name: 90-90's
desc: 90-90's are a mobility exercise designed to improve hip mobility and flexibility. This exercise involves positioning your hips and knees at 90-degree angles to work on hip external and internal rotation.
steps: Make sure your hip, knee, and ankles are all positioned in 90 degree angles
Drop your chest down to your front knee as you breath out, feeling a deep stretch behind your hip
Slowly come back to an upright seated position as you breathe in.
Get creative to feel an even bigger stretch. Try "scanning" the ground as you drop your chest down, and continue to stretch in the direction you feel the most tension

name: Ab In and Outs - Hand Support
Ab In and Outs - No Hands
Ab Rollouts
desc: Ab Rollouts are one of the most challenging ab exercises I'll ever prescribe for clients
cues: Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the movement.
Roll out slowly and with control, avoiding sagging or arching your back.
Exhale as you roll out, inhale as you return.
Only extend as far as you can maintain proper form.
steps: Kneel on the floor with the ab wheel in front of you, holding it with both hands.
Engage your core and slowly roll the wheel forward, extending your body into a straight line.
Go as far forward as you can without arching your back or collapsing your hips.
Use your core muscles to pull yourself back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Ab Triples
desc: One of my favourite exercises to target your abs and obliques.
cues: Keep your core tight like you're going to be poked in the stomach
Exhale while you bring your chest up, squeezing your abs
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and secure your toes under a pair of dumbbells or bottom of a couch.
Place your hands behind your ears or cross your hands over your chest.
Perform a sit-up, exhaling as you squeeze your abs.
Lower yourself back down.
Perform another sit-up but rotate to one side to emphasize using your obliques in a twisting motion.
Lower yourself back down.
Sit-up, twisting in the opposite direction and lowering yourself back on the ground.
Perform as many triples as are prescribed

name: Active Plank
desc: The Active Plank is an intense variation of the traditional plank that involves way more core activation, making it much harder to maintain!
cues: Think about pushing your elbows down towards your toes, and your toes up towards your elbows.
Imagine you're suspended in the air facing downward while trying to pinch a sheet of drywall between your elbows and toes. Weird but it works.
steps: Begin in a plank position with your elbows directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
DRIVE your elbows down towards your toes while you drive your toes up towards your elbows. (you should be shaking almost immediately)

name: Alternating Step Back Lunges
desc: Alternating Step-Back Lunges are a dynamic lower body exercise that can help improve leg strength, balance, and coordination.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
PULL yourself forward using your front leg to emphasize your hamstring and glute
Keep your front knee over your ankle.
steps: Start by standing with your feet hip-width apart, holding 2 dumbbells down by your sides if appropriate.
Take a step back with your strongest leg, lowering your body by bending your front knee until your back knee hovering just above the ground. This should ideally be one smooth motion
Ensure your front knee stays over your ankle, and is at a 90-degree angle. Your back knee should also end up at a 90-degree angle.
Pull through your front heel using your hamstring and glute to return to the starting position.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement, with your chest open and core engaged.
Alternate legs each repetition.

name: Alternating Stepups
desc: Alternating Stepups are an effective lower body exercise that targets the quads, hamstrings, and glutes, while working a ton on your lower body stability.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Keep an even center of pressure across your plant foot “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
When stepping up, keep your kneecap pointing in the direction of your middle toes. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
Try to be as quite as possible when touching your back foot down.
steps: Stand facing an elevated platform or bench.
Step onto the platform with one foot, ensuring your whole foot is firmly planted.
Push through your full foot to lift your other leg to the point it's hovering over the platform.
Step back down with control and return to the starting position. Your foot should touch down very softly.
Alternate feet each repetition until complete.

name: Alternating V-Ups
desc: I personally think Alternating V-Ups are a super fun, more advanced core exercise.
cues: Control the movement and avoid swinging your legs or upper body.
Engage your core muscles throughout the entire exercise.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs fully extended and your arms stretched out to your sides.
Simultaneously lift one arm and the opposite leg, reaching your fingers towards your toes.
Alternate reaching your left hand towards your right toes and your right hand towards your left toes.
Pause at the top of the movement and focus on feeling the contraction in your abs.
Slowly lower your upper body and legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on maintaining proper form and controlled breathing.

name: Back Extension (Glute Focus)
desc: Back Extensions with a Glute Focus a high rep exercise that will make your glutes BURN.
cues: Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement like you're trying to crack a walnut
Think about pushing your feet out and back
steps: Position yourself on the back extension apparatus with your feet secured and your hips at the edge of the pad.
Point your toes out at a 45-degree angle and round your upper back to emphasize your glutes through the movement
Lower your upper body toward the ground, maintaining a curve in your upper back.
Squeeze your glutes to lift your upper body back up to meet parallel with the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Back Extension Machine
desc: The Machine Back Extension targets the lower back muscles along with engaging the glutes and hamstrings.
cues: Keep you core braced the entire time, avoiding any excess bending of your back
Keep you butt pressed into the corner of the seat throughout the movement
Control the descent slowly and smoothly to maximize muscle engagement.
steps: Adjust the machine according to the manufacturer's instructions (usually printed on the side of the machine)
Sit in the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet securely placed on the footrest. Your butt should be in the corner of the seat
Grasp the handles of the machine, if available, for stability.
Exhale and push against the back pad, maintaining a braced core.
Inhale as you slowly return to the starting position, ensuring a controlled movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Alternating Bent Over Rows
desc: Alternating Bent Over Band Rows are an effective exercise for targeting your back and biceps. Using resistance bands adds a unique challenge to this movement, helping you build strength and muscle in your upper body while working each side independently.
cues: Pull your shoulder blades down and back, pretending to squeeze a pencil between them
Keep your chest open and proud.
Initiate the row by pulling one elbow back at a time, starting with your weaker arm
steps: Begin in a standing position with the resistance band securely anchored under your feet
Hinge at your hips to bend forward, maintaining a flat back and a slight bend in your knees.
Hold the band with both hands, arms extended downward.
Pull one elbow back, bringing your hand toward your hip, and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Alternate sides, focusing on one arm at a time.
Pause at the top of each row, feeling the contraction in your back muscles.
Slowly return each arm to the starting position, maintaining tension in the band.

name: Band Ankle Distraction
desc: The Banded Ankle Distraction is a mobility exercise that helps create some "space" in your ankle joint, by loosening your ankles muscles, tendons and ligaments.
steps: Anchor a resistance band to a sturdy object at ankle height.
Make sure you're not tensing your foot or lower leg, the band should be creating a little space in the joint
Move slowly through the sequence.

name: Band Assisted Chin-Ups (Low Band)
desc: Band Assisted Chin-ups are great for your back and biceps, the band provides variable assistance which means the bottom of the movement will be easier while there's a ton of tension in the band, and much more challenging at the top where there's less tension in the band.
cues: Pinch your shoulders down and back like you're trying to hold a pencil between them
Think about driving your elbows down to your hips, you're hands are just there to connect you with the bar
Stick your chest out proud!
steps: Attach a resistance band across squat rack safety attachments.
Grab onto the bar with an underhand grip before stepping onto the band.
Initiate the chin-up by pulling your chest toward the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you pull.
Continue the movement until your chin is above the bar.
Slowly control the descent, lowering yourself back to the starting position.

name: Band Assisted Chin-ups (High Anchor)
desc: Band Assisted Chin-ups are great for your back and biceps, the band provides variable assistance which means the bottom of the movement will be easier while there's a ton of tension in the band, and much more challenging at the top where there's less tension in the band.
cues: Pinch your shoulders down and back like you're trying to hold a pencil between them
Think about driving your elbows down to your hips, you're hands are just there to connect you with the bar
Stick your chest out proud!
steps: Attach a resistance band to a pull-up bar or sturdy overhead anchor point.
Grab onto the bar with an underhand grip before stepping one foot into the band
Cross your other foot over the band to secure it in position
Initiate the chin-up by pulling your chest toward the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you pull.
Continue the movement until your chin is above the bar.
Slowly control the descent, lowering yourself back to the starting position.

name: Band Assisted Dips
desc: Band Assisted Dips are a compound exercise that primarily targets the triceps, chest, and shoulders. This variation uses resistance bands to assist in the movement, making it accessible to individuals working on their dip strength.
cues: For more chest activation, lean slightly forward and try to bend the handles towards one another
For more tricep activation, keep your feet a little more forward and focus on extending through your elbows
Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're pinching a pencil between your shoulder blades or like you're trying to put your shoulder blades in your back pockets
steps: Secure a resistance band on parallel bars or a dip station.
Place your knees or feet in the band for assistance.
Maintain an upright posture with your chest up.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Go as low as your flexibility allows while keeping your shoulders down and back.
Push up through your palms to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Assisted Pull-Ups (Low Anchor)
desc: Band Assisted Pull-ups are great for your back and biceps, and will emphasize developing the outer fibers of your lats, giving the illusion of a smaller waist. The band provides variable assistance which means the bottom of the movement will be easier while there's a ton of tension in the band, and much more challenging at the top where there's less tension in the band.
cues: Pinch your shoulders down and back like you're trying to hold a pencil between them
Think about driving your elbows down to your hips, you're hands are just there to connect you with the bar
Stick your chest out proud!
steps: Attach a resistance band to the safeties in a squat rack.
Grab onto the bar with an underhand grip before stepping one foot into the band
Initiate the pull-up by pulling your chest toward the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue the movement until your chin is above the bar.
Slowly control the descent, lowering yourself back to the starting position.

name: Band Assisted Pull-ups (High Anchor)
desc: Band Assisted Pull-ups are great for your back and biceps, and will emphasize the outside fibers of your lats, which will make your waist look smaller. The band provides variable assistance which means the bottom of the movement will be easier while there's a ton of tension in the band, and much more challenging at the top where there's less tension in the band.
cues: Pinch your shoulders down and back like you're trying to hold a pencil between them
Think about driving your elbows down to your hips, you're hands are just there to connect you with the bar
Stick your chest out proud!
steps: Attach a resistance band to a pull-up bar or sturdy overhead anchor point.
Grab onto the bar with an overhand grip before stepping one foot into the band
Cross your other foot over the band to secure it in position
Initiate the pull-up by pulling your chest toward the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue the movement until your chin is above the bar.
Slowly control the descent, lowering yourself back to the starting position.

name: Band Backpack Distraction
desc: The Banded Shoulder Distraction is a mobility exercise that helps create some "space" in your shoulder joint, by loosening your shoulder's muscles, tendons and ligaments.
steps: Anchor a resistance band to a sturdy object at knee height.
Make sure you're not tensing your shoulder, the band should be creating a little space in the joint
Move slowly through the sequence, if you find one movement feels better than the others, do more of that movement!

name: Band Bent Over Rows
desc: The Band Bent Over Band Row is an effective exercise for targeting your back and biceps. Using resistance bands adds a unique challenge to this movement, making the top of the movement especially challenging
cues: Squeeze your shoulder blades together like you're trying to pinch a pencil.
Keep your chest open and proud.
Think about driving through your elbows, your hands are "hooks"
steps: Begin in a standing position with the resistance band securely under your feet
Hinge at your hips to bend forward, maintaining a flat back and a slight bend in your knees.
Hold the band with both hands, arms extended downward.
Pull your elbows back, bringing your hands toward your hips, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the top of the movement, feeling the contraction in your back muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining tension in the band.

name: Band Bent Over Rows (With Flared Elbows)
desc: The Band Bent Over Band Row is an effective exercise for targeting your back and biceps. This version with flared elbows focuses on your upper back and rear delts. Using resistance bands adds a unique challenge to this movement, making the top of the movement especially challenging.
cues: Squeeze your shoulder blades together like you're trying to pinch a pencil.
Keep your chest open and proud.
Think about driving through your elbows, your hands are "hooks"
steps: Begin in a standing position with the resistance band securely under your feet
Hinge at your hips to bend forward, maintaining a flat back and a slight bend in your knees.
Hold the band with both hands, arms extended downward.
Pull your elbows up in line with your shoulders, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the top of the movement, feeling the contraction in your upper back muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining tension in the band.
subs: Dumbbell Bent Over Row with Wide Elbows

name: Band Bicep 21's
desc: Band Bicep 21's are a variation of the traditional 21's, using a resistance band. This exercise consists of three distinct movements targeting the full bicep.
cues: Keep tension on the band throughout all parts of the exercise.
Focus on maintaining good form, especially as fatigue sets in.
Keep your elbows stationary and close to your body.
steps: Stand on the middle of the resistance band, feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the ends of the band with your hands, palms facing up.
Perform 7 half curls from the bottom to the midpoint.
Follow with 7 half curls from the midpoint to the top.
Finish with 7 full range of motion curls.
Ensure smooth transitions between each phase.
Complete the sequence for one set.

name: Band Bicep Curls
desc: The Band Bicep Curl is a great variation that you can do almost anywhere.
cues: Keep your elbows stationary at your sides throughout the movement.
Focus on squeezing your biceps at the top of the curl.
Maintain a controlled tempo, avoiding using momentum.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, stepping on the middle of the band.
Hold each end of the band with your hands, palms facing up.
Curl your hands towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Pause at the top of the curl.
Slowly lower your hands back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Bicep Stretch
desc: The Band Bicep Stretch is an effective dynamic stretching exercise that targets the biceps, helping to improve flexibility and range of motion in your arms.
steps: Anchor a light-medium resistance band at head height
Wrap the resistance band around your wrist, and turn your body away from the anchor point, starting to feel a stretch across your chest and shoulders
Rotate your wrist as much as you can in either direction while keeping tension in the band

name: Band Face Pulls
desc: Banded Face Pulls are a fantastic exercise for strengthening the upper back and rear deltoid muscles, promoting better posture.
cues: Pull your shoulder blades back and down as if you're trying to pinch a pencil between them.
Maintain a proud chest.
Think about putting your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
steps: Secure a resistance band at head height, either by wrapping it around a sturdy anchor or using a door attachment.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the band with both hands, palms facing down and your thumbs wrapped around it.
Take a step back to create tension in the band.
Keep your core engaged and maintain an upright posture.
Begin by pulling the band above your head with your elbows at 90 degrees, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together. (Alternatively you can pull the band to your nose)
Keep your elbows high and out to the sides.
Hold the peak contraction for a moment.
Slowly release the band to the starting position with control.
Repeat

name: Band Front Raise
desc: The Band Front Raise is a shoulder-strengthening exercise that primarily targets the front deltoids. This exercise utilizes resistance bands for resistance and can help improve shoulder strength and stability.
cues: Imagine you're holding a heavy pitcher of "water" that you're raising to cheers someone far away
Squeeze your core to maintain balance
steps: Stand on a resistance band with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Maintain a strong grip on the band with both hands, palms facing together.
Keep your core engaged for stability.
Lift the band forward, extending your arms, while maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Hold for a moment, feeling the contraction in your front deltoids.
Slowly lower the band back to the starting position with control.

name: Band Hip Distraction
desc: The Banded Hip Distraction is a mobility exercise that helps create some "space" in your hip joint, by loosening your hip's muscles, tendons and ligaments.
steps: Anchor a resistance band to a sturdy object at knee height.
Make sure you're not tensing your hip, the band should be creating a little space in the joint.
Move slowly through the sequence, if you find one movement feels better than the others, do more of that movement!

name: Band Lat Pulldown
desc: Banded Lat Pulldowns are a fantastic exercise for targeting the muscles of your back, specifically your latissimus dorsi.
cues: Sit with an upright posture, engaging your core.
Grip the resistance band with both hands, palms facing forward.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back, as if trying to squeeze them together.
Initiate the movement by pulling your elbows down towards your sides.
Focus on contracting your lats throughout the motion.
steps: Begin by attaching the resistance band to an overhead anchor point.
Sit on a bench or chair facing the anchor point.
Hold the band with both hands, arms fully extended overhead.
Keep your chest up and core engaged.
Pull your elbows down and back, bringing your hands towards your chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return your hands to the starting position, maintaining tension in the band.

name: Band Lateral Raise
desc: The Band Lateral Raise is an effective exercise for targeting the side deltoids. It involves using resistance bands to work on shoulder strength and stability.
cues: Keep your elbows high throughout.
Imagine you're holding a pitcher of water in each hand that you're trying to pour out.
steps: Stand on a resistance band with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the band with both hands, palms facing your thighs.
Keep your core engaged and maintain an upright posture.
Lift the band outward to shoulder level, leading with your elbows.
Hold for a moment, feeling the contraction in your side deltoids.
Slowly lower the band back to your thighs with control.

name: Band Pallof Press
desc: The Band Pallof Press is an antirotation exercise that strengthens your core.
cues: Maintain a stable and controlled posture throughout the movement.
Engage your core muscles to resist the rotational force from the band.
steps: Secure a resistance band to a stationary object just below chest height.
Hold the band with both hands and step away to create tension.
Stand perpendicular to the anchor point, maintaining a stable stance.
Push the band straight out in front of your chest, resisting the rotational force.
Hold the position for a few seconds, focusing on maintaining a stable and engaged core.
Slowly return the band back to your chest in a controlled manner.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on maintaining proper form and controlled breathing.

name: Band Pull Apart
desc: The Band Pull Apart is an effective exercise for strengthening the muscles in your upper back, shoulders, and rear deltoids while improving your posture.
steps: Begin by holding a resistance band with both hands in front of your chest, arms extended.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and a slight bend in your knees.
Keep your core engaged and your back straight.
Exhale as you pull the band apart by moving your hands outward, away from each other.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together as you perform the movement.
Inhale as you return your hands to the starting position with control.
Make sure you're keeping your arms nearly straight for the entire movement!

name: Band Pullover
desc: Band Pullovers are a great isolation exercise for activating your back.
cues: Stick your chest out the entire time
Think about SQUEEZING your lats as you bring the band down
steps: Anchor a resistance band securely to a stable object around head height
Walk back so there's tension in the band, and hinge your hips backwards
Hold the band with both hands, palms facing together, and arms extended overhead.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout.
Lower your arms backward and downward in a controlled motion to the outside of your hips.
Squeeze your lats for a couple seconds before returning to the starting position.
Maintain tension in the band throughout the exercise.

name: Band Rear Delt Fly
desc: The Banded Bent Over Rear Delt Fly is an effective exercise for targeting the rear deltoid muscles, which are located in the back of the shoulders. It helps improve shoulder strength and posture.
cues: Pull your shoulder blades back and down as if you're trying to pinch a pencil between them.
Maintain a proud chest.
Think about keeping a very slight bend in your elbows, your arms should be nearly straight
steps: Stand on the center of a resistance band with your feet hip-width apart.
Hold one end of the band in each hand.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at your hips to lean forward, keeping your back straight.
Keep your arms nearly straight the entire movement.
Engage your core for stability.
Begin by squeezing your shoulder blades together as you lift your arms out to the sides.
Focus on keeping a proud chest, and trying to feel your rear delts work
Hold the peak contraction for a moment.
Slowly return to the starting position with control.
Repeat

name: Band Seated Row
desc: The Seated Band Row is a great exercise for strengthening your entire back (especially your lats) and improving overall posture. It involves pulling a resistance band towards your torso while seated, targeting key upper body muscles.
cues: Pull your shoulder blades back and down as if you're trying to pinch a pencil between them.
Maintain a proud chest
Drive your elbows back, thinking of your hands as hooks
Think about putting your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
muscles: Mid Back (Rhomboids and mid & lower trapezius)

name: Band Shoulder Distraction
desc: The Banded Shoulder Distraction is a mobility exercise that helps create some "space" in your shoulder joint, by loosening your shoulder's muscles, tendons and ligaments.
steps: Anchor a resistance band to a sturdy object at head height.
Make sure you're not tensing your shoulder, the band should be creating a little space in the joint
Move slowly through the sequence, if you find one movement feels better than the others, do more of that movement!

name: Band Shoulder External Rotation
desc: Choose a light band here, don't push into pain

name: Band Shoulder Press - CM
desc: The Band Shoulder Press is a shoulder-strengthening exercise that targets the deltoid muscles. This exercise uses resistance bands to provide resistance and can help improve shoulder strength and stability.
cues: Keep your abs and glutes SQUEEZED the entire time
Finish with your head "in the window", not through the window (the window created by your arms and the band)
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears
steps: Stand on a resistance band with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the band with both hands at shoulder height.
Maintain a strong grip on the band.
Keep your core engaged for stability, and your shoulders down away from your ears.
Press the band upward, extending your arms overhead.
Lock out your elbows at the top of the press.
Hold for a moment, feeling the contraction in your shoulders.
Slowly lower the band back to shoulder height with control.

name: Band Single Arm Seated Row
desc: The Seated Single Arm Band Row is an effective exercise for targeting your back and biceps. It's great for balancing out the body since it's a unilateral movement.
cues: Pull your shoulder blades back and down as if you're trying to pinch a pencil between them.
Keep your chest open and proud throughout the movement.
Imagine driving your elbow back, thinking of your hand as a hook
steps: Sit with a straight back and core engaged.
Hold the resistance band with one hand, palm facing down.
Start with your arm fully extended and pull the band towards your hip.
Squeeze your shoulder blade as you pull.
Keep your elbow close to your body during the pull.
Slowly return to the starting position with control.

name: Band Sissy Squats
desc: Band Sissy Squats are a quad BURNER. They promote knee stability and are great for developing your lower body.
cues: Think about letting the band pull your knees forward and then STRETCH the band back as you come up
Keep your chest back behind your knees
steps: Attach a resistance band to an anchor point (a squat rack works great) at knee height)
Secure the band around the back of your legs just below your knees. Back up so there's tension in the band
While keeping your feet flat on the floor, squat your butt down to your heels and let your knees come forward, releasing tension on the band.
Keep your chest back as you squat down
When you get to the bottom of your squat, push through your full foot and think about STRETCHING the band to get maximum quad activation
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Tricep Extensions
desc: Band Tricep Extensions are one of my favourite tricep exercises to do at home or at the gym. One thing to keep in mind is the further you are the more challenging it will be.
cues: Pretend you're trying to hold a stack of papers underneath your armpits, and you're trying not to let them fall
Control the tension of the band throughout the exercise.
Maintain a proud chest
steps: Secure a resistance band to a high anchor point.
While holding the band in both hands, take a couple steps back away from the anchor.
While keeping your elbows tight to your body, extend your arms fully, stretching the band.
Slowly return to the starting position, with your elbows back while maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.

name: Band Upright Row
desc: The Band Upright Row is a somewhat contentious exercise that works on your shoulders and traps.
cues: Drive your elbows up, thinking of your hands merely as hooks
Maintain a proud chest
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears
steps: Stand on a resistance band with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the band with both hands, palms facing you.
Keep your core engaged and maintain an upright posture.
Pull the band upward toward your chin, leading with your elbows.
Lift until your hands are just below your chin.
Hold for a moment, squeezing your shoulders.
Slowly lower the band back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Wood Chop
desc: The Band Wood Chop is a dynamic rotational exercise that targets your core
cues: Control the movement throughout the entire range of motion.
Think about rotating through your midsection, not your hips
steps: Anchor the band at chest level.
Stand perpendicular to the band with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Grasp the band with both hands and step away from the anchor point until there's tension in the band
With straight arms, rotate your midsection to bring the band away from the anchor point.
Control the movement as you rotate back towards the anchor point.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, before switching to the other side.

name: Bands Glute Bridge
desc: The Band Glute Bridge is a great way to activate your glutes and build a stronger mind muscle connection.
cues: Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement like you're trying to squeeze a walnut.
Push your knees out against the band.
Think about driving through your heels to get more glute activation.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground, place a resistance band just above your knees (you can also add one under the knees as well.
Push your heels into the ground and raise your hips toward the ceiling. Push out your knees and focus on squeezing your glutes.
Lower your hips back down to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Bar Cable Bicep Curls
desc: Bar Cable Bicep Curls use a cable machine with a bar attachment to provide constant tension on the biceps, enhancing muscle growth and strength.
cues: Keep your elbows glued to your sides like you're holding a stack of paper under your armpits
Fully extend your arms at the bottom, but avoid locking the elbows.
steps: Stand in front of a cable machine with the pulley set to the bottom position.
Attach a straight or EZ curl bar to the cable.
Grip the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart and stand tall.
Curl the bar towards your chest, keeping your elbows stationary.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Bar Cable Tricep Extension
desc: Tricep Pushdown with a bar attachment is a great isolation exercise for the triceps. Stand in front of the cable machine with a bar attachment on the high pulley. Grasp the bar, elbows tucked to your sides. Push the bar downward by extending your elbows, fully straightening your arms, then return to the starting position.
steps: Keep your upper arms stationary throughout the movement (pretend you're holding pieces of paper under your armpits)
Maintain a strong core and a slight forward lean to isolate the triceps
Squeeze your triceps at the bottom of the movement for maximum contraction.
Use a controlled tempo, both when pushing down and releasing the weight.
subs: Tricep Pushdown with a straight rope attachment.

name: Barbell Back Squats
desc: Barbell back squats are considered "the king of all exercises. It's TERRIFIC for developing lower body strength and musculature.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Keep an even center of pressure across the “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Keep your kneecaps pointing in the direction of your middle toe. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
Screw your feet into the floor, left foot screwing in counterclockwise and right foot screwing in clockwise
Pull the barbell into your back, keeping your elbows in
steps: Set up the barbell in the squat rack at chest height, and the safeties at an appropriate height in case you need to bail on a squat.
Grab the bar just outside shoulder width
Position the barbell on your upper back NOT on your neck. Pull the barbell into your back
Step your feet directly under the bar and look straight ahead

subs: Seated Cable Rows with Single Arm

name: Cable Single Arm Row
desc: The Single Arm Cable Row targets your back muscles, particularly the lats and rhomboids, with a focus on unilateral strength and muscle balance.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Drive through your elbows, thinking of your hands as hooks
steps: Attach a single handle to a cable row machine.
Grasp the handle with your weaker arm first, keeping your arm extended and your palm facing downward.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the movement.
Pull the handle towards your hip, leading with your elbow and focusing on engaging your back muscles, while rotating your palm upward.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the peak of the movement, slightly rotating your chest in the direction of your working arm.
Control the handle back to the starting position, fully extending your arm, and rotating your palm so it's facing down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Cable Tricep Pushdowns (Rope)
desc: The Cable Tricep Pushdown with a rope attachment is a great isolation exercise for the triceps. Stand in front of the cable machine with a rope attachment on the high pulley. Grasp the rope ends with a neutral grip, elbows tucked to your sides. Push the rope downward by extending your elbows, fully straightening your arms, then return to the starting position.
steps: Keep your upper arms stationary throughout the movement (pretend you're holding pieces of paper under your armpits)
Maintain a strong core and a slight forward lean to isolate the triceps
Squeeze your triceps at the bottom of the movement for maximum contraction.
Use a controlled tempo, both when pushing down and releasing the weight.
subs: Tricep Pushdown with a straight bar attachment.

name: Cable Wood Chop
desc: The Cable Wood Chop is a dynamic rotational exercise that targets the core muscles.
cues: Control the movement throughout the entire range of motion.
Engage your core muscles to generate the rotational force from the cable.
Think about rotating through your midsection, keeping your hips steady
steps: Set the cable to chest height.
Stand perpendicular to the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Grasp the handle with both hands and step away from the machine until the weight is lifted
With straight arms, rotate your midsection to bring the handle away from the machine.
Control the movement as you rotate back towards the machine.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, before switching to the other side.

name: Calf Raise on Leg Press
desc: The Single Leg Leg Press is a great way to isolate each of your legs, making sure they develop at the same rate
cues: Push your foot through the platform
Make sure your knee cap points in the same direction as your toes (not caving in)
Keep an even center of pressure across the “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
steps: Sit on the leg press machine with your back against the seat and your weaker foot placed on the platform.
Push the platform away from you, and release the safeties.
Bend your knee to slowly lower the platform toward your body, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Push the weight back up, not quite fully locking out your knee.
Repeat for the prescribed number of reps before reengaging the safeties and switching to the other leg.

name: Calf Stretch - CM
desc: This version of the calf stretch uses a wall for support to effectively stretch the calf muscles, particularly the gastrocnemius and soleus. It's a great stretch for improving flexibility and relieving tightness in the calves.
cues: Try stretching your leg with a straight knee, and with a slightly bent knee to stretch more parts of your calf.
Ensure your front leg is slightly bent and positioned for stability.
Lean into the wall gently to increase the stretch.
Maintain a straight line from your back heel to your head.
steps: Stand facing a wall with your hands placed on it at shoulder height.
Step one foot back, keeping it straight with the heel flat on the ground.
Bend your front knee slightly, keeping your back leg straight.
Press your hips forward and push against the wall to feel a stretch in your back calf.
You can try putting your support leg in different positions to feel different stretches
Switch legs and repeat.
subs: Step Calf Stretch (using a step or curb)

name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
desc: I like this variation of knee raises since it takes your grip strength out of the equation.
cues: Focus on using your abdominals to lift your knees, rather than swinging.
Keep your movements controlled and deliberate.
Exhale as you raise your knees, engaging your core more intensely.
steps: Position yourself in the Captain's Chair, back against the pad, gripping the handles.
Start with legs hanging down and core engaged.
Bend your knees and lift them towards your chest.
Lift as high as you can while maintaining control.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Captain's Chair Leg Raises
desc: I like this variation of leg raises since it takes your grip strength out of the equation.
cues: Focus on using your abdominals to lift your legs, rather than swinging.
Keep your movements controlled and deliberate.
Exhale as you raise your legs, engaging your core more intensely.
steps: Position yourself in the Captain's Chair, back against the pad, gripping the handles.
Start with legs hanging down and core engaged.
Keeping your knees straight, lift your legs as high as you can while maintaining control.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cardio of Choice
desc: Cardio of your choice! A bike, elliptical, treadmill, stairmaster, or rower are all great options.

name: Cat-Cow
desc: The Cat-Cow Stretch is a dynamic yoga-inspired exercise that promotes spinal flexibility and mobility. It alternates between two poses, resembling the arching and rounding of a cat's back and a cow's back.
steps: Begin on your hands and knees in a tabletop position, with your wrists directly under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Inhale as you arch your back, lifting your head and tailbone towards the ceiling. Your belly drops down, resembling a cow's back (Cow Pose).
Exhale as you round your back, tucking your chin and tailbone, and drawing your navel toward your spine, resembling a cat's back (Cat Pose).
Continue to flow between these two poses, synchronizing your breath with the movement.
Inhale for Cow Pose and exhale for Cat Pose.
subs: Child's Pose to Upward Facing Dog

name: Cheat Curls
desc: The Barbell Cheat Curl allows for using heavier weights by incorporating a slight body movement. This exercise helps in overloading the biceps for strength and mass gain.
cues: Start the curl with a slight forward momentum from the hips.
Keep the movement controlled; avoid excessive swinging.
Focus on lowering the weight slowly to maximize the eccentric phase.
Keep your chest up and shoulders back throughout the movement.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip.
Slightly lean forward.
Use a controlled swing to start the curl, lifting the barbell towards your chest. Avoid bending your back into extension.
Lower the barbell back down with control, focusing on the bicep muscle.
Repeat for the desired number of reps, focusing on the controlled lowering phase.

name: Chest Stretch - CM
desc: This Chest Stretch is phenomenal for opening up your pecs and shoulders, while activating your back muscles to maintain good posture
steps: Find a squat rack, door frame, or corner of a wall
Put one forearm flat against the wall above shoulder height
Turn your chest away from the wall, feeling a stretch across your upper body

While keeping your elbow flat against the support, lift your hand away from the support like you're about to give it a high five and hold that position for a couple seconds. You should feel your upper back and shoulder muscles working in this position
Sink deeper into the stretch and repeat

name: Chest Supported T-Bar Row
desc: The T-Bar Row is a great exercise for developing your entire back.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Drive through your elbows, thinking of your hands as hooks
steps: Adjust the chest pad to the appropriate height and position yourself with your chest against the pad and your feet planted firmly on the floor or the platform attached to the machine.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip.
Pull the handles towards your lower chest, leading with your elbows and focusing on engaging your back muscles.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the peak of the movement.
Control the handles back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Chest Trigger Point
desc: The Chest Trigger Point helps to alleviate tension and discomfort in your across your chest and shoulders and increases range of motion
steps: Begin by pinning a lacross ball against a squat rack where your chest meets your shoulder (see video)
Begin rolling back and forth in the area looking for tender spots
Once you find a tender spot, try to add pressure to the area using the lacross ball while leaving your muscle relaxed
Spend 5-10 seconds relaxing into the position, then make very small movements over the tender spot for 5-10 seconds
To intensify the trigger point, your can lift your arm directly overhead and then across your body, continuing to look for tender spots
Find another tender spot, and repeat

name: Childs Pose to Upward Facing Dog
desc: Transitioning from Child's Pose to Upward Facing Dog is a yoga sequence that combines two complementary poses to enhance flexibility, mobility, and strength in the spine, shoulders, and lower back.
steps: Begin in Child's Pose. Kneel on the floor with your knees spread apart. Sit back onto your heels, extending your arms forward and lowering your chest toward the floor.

From Child's Pose, slide forward and transition into Upward Facing Dog. Roll your body forward and place your palms on the ground beside your ribs. Press through your palms, lifting your chest and upper body off the floor.
Extend your arms fully, keeping your shoulders down and away from your ears. Arch your back gently, opening your chest and stretching your abdominal muscles.
Lift your hips slightly off the ground, engaging your core muscles.
Keep your thighs and the tops of your feet on the ground. Look forward or slightly upward, keeping your neck in a neutral position.
Hold Upward Facing Dog for a few breaths, feeling the stretch in your spine and the engagement of your chest and shoulders.
To transition back to Child's Pose, pushing your hips back while reaching your arms as far forward as you can and lowering your forehead to the floor

name: Chin-Ups
desc: Chin-Ups are a fantastic upper body exercise that targets your back and biceps. To perform a Chin-Up, hang from a horizontal bar with your palms facing you and your hands shoulder-width apart. Pull your body upward until your chin clears the bar, then lower yourself back down with control.
steps: Begin with a dead hang to fully engage your muscles before pulling up.
Keep your core tight
Focus on bringing your chest toward the bar, not just your chin.
Lower yourself in a controlled manner, resisting the urge to drop.

name: Close Grip Knee Push Up
desc: Close Grip Knee Pushups are a modified version of knee pushups that target the triceps.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Keep your elbows tight to your body
Think about screwing your hands into the floor, left hand screwing in counterclockwise and right hand screwing in clockwise
steps: Kneel on the ground with your knees hip-width apart.
Place your hands close together, directly under your shoulders.
Maintain a straight line from your head to your knees throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Descend until your chest is just above the ground, or as far as your flexibility allows.
Push up through your palms to return to the starting position.
Engage your core for stability throughout the exercise.

name: Close Grip Push Up
desc: Close-Grip Pushups are a variation of traditional pushups that target the triceps more intensely.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Keep your elbows tucked into your sides and SQUEEZE your triceps at the top
steps: Begin in a standard pushup position.
Place your hands directly under your shoulders.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Go as low as your flexibility allows while keeping your shoulders down and back.
Push up through your full hand to return to the starting position.

name: Combat Base Stretch
desc: The Combat Base Ankle Stretch is a dynamic stretching exercise for the calves and ankles
steps: Begin in a kneeling position with one foot planted
Keeping your knelt foot flat on the ground, push your knee past your toes
In this stretched position, try to pull your toes up off the ground, feeling the front of your shin activate. Repeat 3 times.
Ebb and flow deeper into the stretch, trying to pull your toes off the ground

name: Concentration Curls
desc: Concentration Curls are a focused bicep exercise that prevents momentum, promoting intense muscle engagement. It's performed while seated, isolating the bicep on one arm at a time.
cues: Keep your upper arm stationary against your inner thigh.
Focus on squeezing the bicep at the top of each curl.
Avoid swinging or using your back
Fully extend your arm on each repetition.
steps: Sit on the edge of a bench, legs spread, with a dumbbell in one your weakest hand to start.
Lean forward slightly, resting your tricep on the inner thigh of the same side.
Curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder.
Focus on isolating the bicep muscle throughout the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Complete all reps on one arm before switching to the other.

name: Contralateral Bulgarian Split Squats
desc: The Contralateral Bulgarian Split Squat is a powerful unilateral lower body exercise that targets your full lower body and places more emphasis on the outside of your glutes than other split squats. They promote balance, stability, and muscle development. It's considered one of the best lower body exercises there is.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Keep an even center of pressure across the “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Keep your forward kneecap pointing in the direction of your middle toes. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
steps: Stand a couple of feet in front of a bench or platform, facing away from it.
Place the top of one foot on the bench or platform behind you, ensuring your front foot is a comfortable distance away.
Hold a dumbbell in the opposite hand to the foot you have forward.
Lower your body down by bending your front knee, while keeping your foot flat on the ground
Lower your body until your rear knee is just above the ground.
Push through your full foot to return to the top position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: Conventional Deadlift
desc: The Conventional Deadlift works virtually every muscle in your body, but focuses mostly on your hamstrings, glutes, and lower back.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Keep an even center of pressure across the “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Keep your kneecaps pointing in the direction of your middle toes. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
Screw your feet into the floor, left foot screwing in counterclockwise and right foot screwing in clockwise
“Spread the floor” (you can imagine standing on wet newspaper that you’re trying to split down the middle)
Squeeze your glutes like you're trying to crush a walnut
Make your armpits disappear by squeezing your triceps into your lats
steps: Stand 1 inch away from the bar with your feet hip distance apart.
With vertical shins, and a neutral spine, reach back with your butt until your hands can reach the bar.
Grab the bar at shoulder width, and try to snap it in half.
Take a breath in like you're going to dive underwater and brace your core

"Pull the slack" out of the bar before bringing your hips forward between your knees and shoulders, maintaining your brace and neutral spine (think of it as a horizontal movement, not a vertical movement)
Pause briefly at the top before reaching your butt back into a hinge pattern, returning the bar to the ground with vertical shins and a neutral spine
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Copenhagen Plank
desc: The Copenhagen Plank is a challenging side plank variation that targets the obliques and adductors (inner thigh muscles), promoting core stability and balance.
cues: Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Maintain a neutral neck and avoid sagging in the hips.
Breathe steadily to maintain balance and stability.
steps: Lie on your side, propping your upper body up on your forearm.
Place your top leg on a bench or a stable elevated surface.
Keep your bottom leg hanging or resting on the ground for support.
Lift your hips off the ground, forming a straight line with your body.
Hold the position for a set duration, then switch sides.

name: Core 4 on the Floor
desc: Core 4 on the Floor is a phenomenal lower body warmup, one of the best ways to cover all of your lower body mobility in one fell swoop
steps: Focus on moving slowly through the movement, and spend more time doing the movements that feel best for you!

name: Crunch - CM
desc: Crunches are an abdominal exercise that focuses on the rectus abdominis muscles, commonly known as the "six-pack." This exercise helps strengthen the core and improve abdominal muscle definition.
cues: Exhale as you contract your abs.
Think about squeezing your rib cage down to your pelvis each rep.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground, hip-width apart.
Place your hands lightly behind your head, without pulling on your neck, or you can cross your arms over your chest.
Engage your core muscles by gently pulling your navel toward your spine.
Lift your upper body off the ground by contracting your abdominal muscles, keeping your lower back flat on the floor.
Exhale as you contract your abs and focus on the crunching motion.
Lower your upper body back down to the ground with control, but don't let your head touch the floor.
Inhale as you lower your upper body.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Curl Up
desc: The Curl Up is an exercise that focuses on strengthening the core muscles while minimizing stress on the spine. This exercise is designed to promote spinal stability.
cues: Keep your lower back in a neutral position throughout the movement.
Squeeze your abs at the top of the movement
steps: Lie on your back with one knee bent and the other leg extended straight.
Place your hands palm down under the natural arch of your lower back for support.
Gently lift your head and shoulders off the ground, maintaining a neutral spine position.
Hold the position for a few seconds, focusing on engaging your abdominal muscles.
Slowly lower your head and shoulders back to the ground in a controlled manner.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then alternate which leg is extended and repeat

name: Cycling Tabata
desc: The classic Tabata protocol — 20 seconds of ultra-intense effort followed by 10 seconds of rest, repeated for 4 minutes (8 cycles) — is a challenging and efficient way to improve both aerobic and anaerobic capacity.
cues: Push hard during the high-intensity intervals, aiming for maximal effort.
Maintain a smooth and controlled pedal stroke, even when fatigued.
Use the rest intervals to recover, slowing down but keeping the pedals moving.
Keep your upper body relaxed and avoid tensing up your shoulders and neck.
steps: Warm up with 3 minutes of moderate-paced cycling to prepare your muscles and cardiovascular system.
Increase the resistance on your bike to a level that allows you to push hard for 20 seconds.
Pedal at maximum effort for 20 seconds, aiming to reach your highest possible speed.
Reduce the speed and resistance for a 10-second rest period. Keep pedaling, but allow your heart rate to come down.
Repeat this cycle of 20 seconds of work followed by 10 seconds of rest for a total of 8 rounds.
Cool down with 3 minutes of easy cycling to help your body recover.
muscles: Lower Body Muscles - Quadriceps, Hamstrings, Calves, Glutes

name: Deadbugs
desc: Deadbugs are a core-strengthening exercise that focuses on improving stability and control. This exercise is effective for targeting the entire core area while minimizing stress on the lower back.
cues: Keep a natural arc in your lower back throughout the movement
Engage your core and breath behind your brace
steps: Lie on your back with your arms extended toward the ceiling and your legs bent at a 90-degree angle.
Slowly lower one arm and the opposite leg toward the ground while maintaining a flexed core and a natural arc in your lower back.
Return to the starting position and repeat the movement on the opposite side.
Maintain a controlled and stable position throughout the exercise.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Decline Oblique Sit-Ups
desc: Decline Bench Oblique Sit-Ups are an effective exercise for targeting the oblique muscles along the sides of the abdomen. Performed on a decline bench, this exercise adds intensity to the traditional sit-up by incorporating a twist to engage the obliques.
cues: Keep your lower back pressed against the bench throughout the lower portion of the movement.
Twist your torso, bringing your elbow towards the opposite knee at the top of the sit-up.
Control your descent back to the starting position.
Engage your core muscles throughout the exercise to maximize effectiveness and protect your spine.
steps: Secure your feet at the top of a decline bench and lie down with your back on the bench.
Place your hands lightly behind your head or across your chest. (or hold a weight against your chest if appropriate)
Engage your core and perform a sit-up, lifting your upper body off the bench.
As you sit up, twist your torso so that one elbow moves towards the opposite knee.
Slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Alternate the twist with each repetition to work both sides of the obliques.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Decline Sit-Ups
desc: Decline Sit-Ups are one of the more intense ab exercises. It puts a ton of tension on your abs in the stretched position which is great for hypertrophy.
cues: Curl your spine up like you're trying to touch your pelvis with your ribs
Control your descent back to the starting position.
Engage your core muscles throughout the exercise to maximize effectiveness and protect your spine.
steps: Secure your feet at the top of a decline bench and lie down with your back on the bench.
Place your hands lightly behind your head or across your chest. (or hold a weight against your chest if appropriate)
Engage your core and perform a sit-up, lifting your upper body off the bench.
Slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Deep Squat Stretch - CM
desc: The Deep Squat Stretch is a versatile lower body stretch that targets the hips, groin, lower back, and ankles. It's an excellent exercise for improving hip mobility and flexibility.
steps: Begin by standing with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Slowly lower your body into a squatting position, keeping your heels on the ground.
As you squat down, gently push your knees outward with your elbows, allowing your hips to open.
Keep your chest up and your back straight, maintaining a neutral spine.
Aim to bring your buttocks as close to your heels as comfortably possible.
If you can't keep your heels on the ground, you can put something under your heels for support (like a couple 10lb plates)

name: Deficit Push-Ups
desc: Deficit Push-ups are a twist on a classic exercises that builds strength in your chest, shoulders, and triceps while also engaging your core for stability. ** You can elevate your hands on plates, push-up handles or anything else that is about 10cm high and will allow your chest to drop lower than it would if you were on the ground
steps: Place your hands on 2 plates or another surface ~10cm high shoulder width apart, your thumbs should be just below your armpits, with your fingers pointing forward
Keeping your elbows at a ~45 degree angle from your body, push you your hands to the top position
Lower yourself down with control

name: Dips
desc: Dips are a great way to target your chest, triceps, and shoulders while building upper body strength.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
To target more chest, think about leaning forward, to target more triceps, think about keeping your feet forward
steps: Position yourself on parallel bars with your arms fully extended.
Lean slightly forward and lower your body by bending your elbows until you feel a deep stretch in your shoulders and chest.
Push yourself back up to the starting position, keeping your chest engaged.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Double Goblet Squats
desc: Double Goblet Squats are an excellent  progression to regular goblet squats that primarily targets your quadriceps, adductors and glutes.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Keep an even center of pressure across the “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Keep your kneecaps pointing in the direction of your middle toes. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
Screw your feet into the floor, left foot screwing in counterclockwise and right foot screwing in clockwise
steps: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your toes pointing outward, holding dumbbells or kettlebells in a front rack position.
Lower into a squat position while keeping your chest up and your back straight.
Ensure your knees are aligned with your toes throughout the movement.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Alternating Chest Press
desc: The Dumbbell Alternating Chest Press is an effective exercise for targeting the chest muscles, emphasizing unilateral strength and stability.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
steps: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, feet flat on the floor.
Hold the dumbbells at chest level with your upper arms at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press one dumbbell upwards (starting with your weaker arm) while keeping the other at chest level.
Slowly bring the raised dumbbell back to your chest, and alternate the pressing motion with your stronger arm.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Alternating Front Raise
desc: The Dumbbell Alternating Front Raise is a shoulder exercise that targets the front deltoids. This exercise involves lifting dumbbells alternately in front of you to work on shoulder strength and stability.
cues: Imagine you're "cheersing" someone far infront of you
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears to help isolate your delts
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Maintain a strong grip on the dumbbells.
Keep your core engaged for stability.
Starting with your weaker arm, lift one dumbbell forward to shoulder level while keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Lower that dumbbell back to your side.
Lift the other dumbbell forward in the same manner.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Repeat, alternating between each arm, for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Alternating Rows
desc: Alternating Bent Over Dumbbell Rows are an effective exercise for targeting your back and biceps. This movement involves lifting one dumbbell at a time while maintaining stability in a bent-over position.
cues: Maintain a flat back throughout the exercise.
Keep your chest open and proud.
Think of your hands merely as hooks, you should be driving back through your elbows
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge at your hips to bend forward, maintaining a flat back.
Keep your knees slightly bent for stability.
Allow the dumbbells to hang down in front of you.
Pull one elbow back at a time starting with your weaker side, lifting one dumbbell towards your hip while the other arm stays extended.
Pause at the top of each row, feeling the contraction in your back and biceps.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the row with the opposite arm.

name: Dumbbell Arnold Press (Seated)
desc: The Dumbbell  Arnold Press is a rotational movement, providing a well-rounded shoulder workout.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Think about finishing the rotation and extension of your arm at the same time
steps: Sit with your feet planted firmly into the ground. Use you legs to help you bring the dumbbells up into position.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder height, with your palm facing towards you.
Keep your core engaged for stability.
Start rotating the dumbbells outward (away from your body) as you press them overhead.
Finish the movement with your wrist stacked directly above your shoulder.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height with control, while rotating them back to the starting position.
Repeat

name: Dumbbell Arnold Press (Standing)
desc: The Dumbbell Arnold Press is a rotational movement, providing a well-rounded shoulder workout.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Think about finishing the rotation and extension of your arm at the same time
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder height, with your palm facing towards you.
Keep your core engaged for stability.
Start rotating the dumbbells outward (away from your body) as you press them overhead.
Finish the movement with your wrist stacked directly above your shoulder.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height with control, while rotating them back to the starting position.
Repeat

name: Dumbbell Bent Over Rear Delt Fly
desc: Bent Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly is an effective exercise for targeting the rear deltoid muscles (the back of your shoulders). To perform this exercise, stand with a dumbbell in each hand, bend at the hips to create a slight forward lean, and keep a soft bend in your knees. Let the dumbbells hang in front of you. With a slight bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the ground, then lower them back down with control.
steps: Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Keep your back straight and core engaged to stabilize your posture.
Focus on squeezing your rear deltoids as you lift the dumbbells.
Lift the dumbbells in a controlled manner, both on the way up and down.
Avoid excessive swinging or using momentum.

name: Dumbbell Bent Over Row (Flared Elbows)
desc: Dumbbell Bent Over Row (Flared Elbows) targets your upper back more than traditional bent over rows which will help with your posture!
cues: Keep your chest open and proud.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears, while pinching them together
Drive out through your elbows, your hands are just hooks
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge at your hips to bend forward, maintaining a flat back.
Keep your knees slightly bent for stability.
Allow the dumbbells to hang down in front of you.
Pull your elbows back and outward, while maintaining a proud chest. Your elbows should track in line with your shoulders
Pause at the top of the movement, feeling the contraction in your back, biceps, and rear deltoids.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.

name: Dumbbell Bent Over Row with Supinated Wrists
desc: The Dumbbell Bent Over Row with Supinated Wrists targets your biceps more than other dumbbell bent over rows while also working a ton on your back.
cues: Keep your chest open and proud.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together like you're holding a pencil between them
Drive back through your elbows and SQUEEZE your back and biceps at the top of each movement
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a supinated grip (palms facing forward).
Hinge at your hips to bend forward, maintaining a flat back.
Keep your knees slightly bent for stability.
Allow the dumbbells to hang down in front of you.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, lifting the dumbbells towards your hips.

desc: The Dumbbell Unilateral Standing Arnold Press is a rotational movement, providing a well-rounded shoulder workout.

Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest

Hold the dumbbells at shoulder height, with your palm facing towards you.
Keep your core engaged for stability.
Starting with your weaker arm, rotate the dumbbell outward (away from your body) as you press it overhead.
Finish the movement with your wrist stacked directly above your shoulder.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to shoulder height with control, while rotating it back to the starting position.
Repeat with your other arm

name: Dumbbell Unilateral Standing Arnold Press (Standing)

name: Dumbbell Unilateral Standing Shoulder Press
desc: The Dumbbell Unilateral Standing Shoulder Press is an excellent exercise for targeting each shoulder independently. It focuses on developing shoulder strength and stability.
