Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder height, with your palms facing forward.
Keep your core engaged for stability.
Starting with your weaker side, press one dumbbell overhead, extending your arm fully.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to shoulder height with control.
Repeat with your opposite hand.

name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
desc: The Dumbbell Bench Wrist Curl is an isolation exercise aimed at strengthening the forearm flexors. This variation of the wrist curl uses a bench to support the forearms, allowing for a focused and effective targeting of the muscles involved.
cues: Keep your forearms flat on the bench throughout the exercise to isolate the wrist movement.
Focus on a full range of motion, extending and curling the wrists fully.
Squeeze your forearms at the top of the movement for a peak contraction.
steps: Sit on one side of a bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing up.
Lay your forearms flat on the bench, with your wrists just beyond the edge.
With your arms stationary, lower the dumbbells towards the floor by extending your wrists.
Curl the dumbbells up by flexing your wrists, lifting as high as comfortably possible.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Z-Press
desc: The Dumbbell Z Press is a seated overhead press variation that targets the shoulders. It requires quite a bit of stability in the core and engages the triceps as well.
cues: Pinch your shoulder blades down and back like you're trying to pinch a pencil between them
Maintain a proud chest the entire movement
SQUEEZE your abs and hands
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs extended wide.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
Keep your back straight and chest up.
Press the dumbbells overhead, stacking your wrists overtop of your shoulders
Lower the weights down to your shoulders with control

name: EZ Bar Curl - CM
desc: The EZ Bar Curl uses an EZ curl bar, which is designed to reduce wrist and forearm strain. This variation of the bicep curl allows for a more comfortable grip, targeting the biceps effectively.
cues: Keep your elbows glued to your sides, pretending you're holding a stack of paper under your armpits
Curl the EZ bar towards your chest with a controlled motion.
Fully extend your arms at the bottom of each curl.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, gripping the EZ bar with an underhand grip.
Keep your elbows stationary, close to your torso.
Curl the bar towards your chest, squeezing your biceps at the top.
Lower the bar slowly back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: EZ Bar Preacher Curls
desc: EZ Bar Preacher Curls are a staple bicep exercise that stress your biceps in a "lengthened position" which is great for muscle growth **These bars usually weigh ~10lbs if you choose an easy bar that you add plates to
cues: Curl the weight up with control, emphasizing the squeeze in the biceps.
Fully extend your arms at the bottom, but avoid locking the elbows.
steps: Sit at the preacher bench, gripping a barbell with an underhand grip.
Place your upper arms on the bench, extending your arms.
Curl the weight towards your shoulders, squeezing the biceps at the top.
Lower the weight back to feel a deep stretch in your biceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Elbows to Hands
desc: The Elbows to Hands exercise is a great way to improve upper body strength and core stability. It's like a dynamic plank variation where you transition from your elbows to your hands, engaging your shoulders and core.
steps: Begin in a forearm plank position with your elbows directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Keep your core engaged and your back flat.
Push up from one elbow to your hand, then the other elbow to your hand, transitioning to a high plank position.
Maintain a stable position as you alternate between the forearm plank and high plank.
Ensure that your shoulders stay over your wrists during the transition.
Alternate which hand you initiate the movement with each rep

name: Elevated Prayer Stretch Dowel
desc: The Elevated Prayer Stretch with a Dowel is a variation of the traditional Prayer Stretch, providing a deeper stretch for the shoulders, upper back, and triceps.
steps: Begin by kneeling on a padded surface or yoga mat.
Holding a dowel or broomstick in an underhand position, place your elbows on a bench
Push your hips away from the bench, leaving your elbows stationary
Drop your chest low to feel a stretch in your back and shoulders
Bring the dowel to the back of your head to feel a stretch in your triceps
Ebb and flow with the stretch, continuing to try stretch into deeper positions

name: Farmer's Walk
desc: Farmer's Carries are a functional and full-body exercise that improves grip strength, core stability, and posture. It's like you're carrying heavy buckets of water, but with weights in your hands.
steps: Stand tall with a weight (dumbbell or kettlebell) in each hand.
Keep your feet hip-width apart.
Engage your core muscles for stability.
Lift the weights off the ground.
Walk forward with short, controlled steps while maintaining an upright posture.
Avoid leaning to one side or rounding your back.
Continue to walk for a designated distance or time.
When finished, safely lower the weights back to the ground.

name: Feet Elevated Pushups
desc: Feet Elevated Pushups are a challenging pushup variation that targets the upper chest and shoulders. .
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Think about screwing your hands into the floor, left hand screwing in counterclockwise and right hand screwing in clockwise
steps: Begin in a standard pushup position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Place your feet on an elevated surface such as a bench, or step.
Maintain a straight line from your head to your heels throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending your elbows.
Descend until your chest is just above the ground, or as far as your flexibility allows.
Push up through your palms to return to the starting position.
Engage your core for stability throughout the exercise.

name: Flutter Kicks - CM
desc: Flutter Kicks are a great ab burner! Try to keep these slow and controlled :)
cues: Engage your core throughout the entire movement.
Control the motion, maintaining a steady and controlled pace.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs fully extended and your arms by your sides or underneath your butt for support.
Engage your core and lift your legs a few inches off the ground.
Begin the movement by alternating lifting each leg up and down in a scissoring motion, similar to a fluttering movement.
Focus on feeling the contraction in your lower abs and maintaining control throughout the exercise.
Continue the fluttering motion for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on maintaining proper form and controlled breathing.

name: Foam Roll Calves
desc: The Calf Foam Roll is a self-myofascial release (SMR) technique that helps relieve muscle tension and improve mobility in the calves. It's an excellent exercise to reduce muscle tightness and soreness.
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Place a foam roller under your calves, with your hands supporting your body weight behind you.
Lift your hips off the ground, supporting your weight on your hands and the foam roller.
Start rolling the foam roller up and down your calves, looking for tender spots
Once you find a tender spot, try to add pressure to the area using the foam roller while leaving your muscle relaxed (you can cross your opposite leg over your shin to add extra pressure)
Spend 5-10 seconds relaxing into the position, then make very small movements over the tender spot for 5-10 seconds
Find another tender spot, and repeat
For bonus points, you can try pointing your toe up towards your face and then away from you while the foam roller is in a tender spot

name: Foam Roll Glutes
desc: Foam rolling the glutes is a self-myofascial release (SMR) technique that helps alleviate tension and discomfort in the gluteal muscles (buttocks). It's an effective exercise for reducing muscle tightness and promoting flexibility in this area.
steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Position the foam roller under one buttock, leaning slightly to the side to place more weight on that glute.
Support your upper body with your hands placed behind you.
Cross one leg over the opposite knee to create more pressure on the glute being rolled.
Begin rolling back and forth along the entire glute looking for tender spots
Once you find a tender spot, try to add pressure to the area using the foam roller while leaving your muscle relaxed
Spend 5-10 seconds relaxing into the position, then make very small movements over the tender spot for 5-10 seconds
Find another tender spot, and repeat

name: Foam Roll IT Band
desc: Foam rolling the IT (iliotibial) bands is a self-myofascial release (SMR) technique that helps alleviate tension and discomfort in the IT bands, which run along the outer thighs. This exercise can reduce muscle tightness and improve mobility in the hip and thigh area.
steps: Begin by lying on your side on the floor with your legs extended.
Position the foam roller under your bottom thigh, near the hip.
Use your arms and the leg not being rolled to support your upper body.
Start rolling the foam roller along the outer thigh, moving from just above the knee to the hip trying to find tender areas
Once you find a tender spot, try to add pressure to the area using the foam roller while leaving your muscle relaxed
Spend 5-10 seconds relaxing into the position, then make very small movements over the tender spot for 5-10 seconds
Find another tender spot, and repeat

name: Foam Roll Lats
desc: Foam rolling your lats is a self-myofascial release (SMR) technique that helps alleviate tension and discomfort across your back. Foam rolling can reduce muscle tightness and improve mobility.
steps: Begin by lying with the foam roller underneath you, running horizontal to your spine
Give yourself a big hug to stretch out your lats
Lean to one side so that the foam roller is only making contact with one of your lats, and isn't on your spine
Start rolling the foam roller along your lats trying to find tender areas
Once you find a tender spot, try to add pressure to the area using the foam roller while leaving your muscle relaxed
Spend 5-10 seconds relaxing into the position, then make very small movements over the tender spot for 5-10 seconds
Find another tender spot, and repeat

name: Foam Roll Subscapularis
desc: The Subscapularis Foam Roll is a self-myofascial release (SMR) exercise that targets the subscapularis muscle, located beneath the shoulder blade just underneath your armpit. Foam rolling your subscapularis helps alleviate tension and increases your shoulder range of motion.
steps: Begin by lying on your side with your legs straight and your foam roller placed horizontally beneath your armpit.
Try to leave your muscles as relaxed as possible while foam rolling
Keep your bottom arm extended straight out for balance.
Begin rolling back and forth along the subscapularis looking for tender spots
Once you find a tender spot, try to add pressure to the area using the foam roller while leaving your muscle relaxed (you can cross your opposite leg over your shin to add extra pressure)
Spend 5-10 seconds relaxing into the position, then make very small movements over the tender spot for 5-10 seconds
Find another tender spot, and repeat

name: Foot Trigger Point
desc: The Foot Trigger Point helps to alleviate tension and discomfort in your feet while increasing range of motion.
steps: Stand in a comfortable and balanced position with your feet hip-width apart.
Place a lacross ball on the floor beneath one foot.
Gently step onto the ball, applying your body weight to it while looking for tender spots

Roll the ball under your foot, focusing on areas that feel tender or tight, which may indicate trigger points. I usually find clients have lots of spots under the sole of their feet and at the base of each toe
Once you find a tender spot, try to add pressure to the area using the lacross ball while leaving your feet relaxed
Spend 5-10 seconds relaxing into the position, then make very small movements over the tender spot for 5-10 seconds
Find another tender spot, and repeat

name: Forward Leg Swings
desc: Forward Leg Swings are a dynamic stretching exercise that focuses on the hip flexors and hamstrings. This exercise helps improve hip mobility and flexibility in the front and back of the thighs.
steps: Stand next to a sturdy support, like a wall or railing, for balance.
Hold onto the support with one hand and keep your core engaged.
Begin by standing tall with your feet together.
Swing one leg forward and upward as high as comfortably possible while keeping it straight or with a slight bend at the knee.
Swing the leg backward, extending it behind you.
Continue to swing your leg back and forth in a controlled motion.

name: Frog Pumps
desc: Frog Pumps are great for glute activation and building a strong mind muscle connection.
cues: Push your feet together
Squeeze your glutes like you're trying to crush a walnut
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent, and the soles of your feet together
Push your feet into the ground and raise your hips toward the ceiling, focusing on squeezing your glutes.
Lower your hips back down to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Front Foot Elevated Split Squat - CM
desc: The Front Foot Elevated Split Squat is an quad BURNER that also works on your glutes and hip stability.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Keep an even center of pressure across your forward foot's “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Keep your front leg's kneecap pointing in the direction of your middle toe. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
steps: Stand with one foot on a slightly elevated surface. A step or couple 45lb plates stacked ontop of one another work perfect. Make sure the surface is stable before beginning.
Hold dumbbells by your side if appropriate.
Lower yourself forward into a lunge position, focusing on keeping your weight on your front foot and maintaining a neutral spine.
Push through your full front foot, squeezing your quad to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.

name: Glute Ham Raise
desc: This is a great exercise for developing your posterior chain. It can be intimidating to start, so I encourage you only to work in a range of motion that you feel comfortable with.

steps: Adjust the GHD machine so that your knees sit comfortably on the pad with your ankles hooked into the back pads. The further forward your knees are, the more difficult this exercise is.

Lower yourself until your body is parallel to the ground, or as far as you can maintain control and proper form.
While maintaining a straight line from your knees through the top of your head, use your hamstrings and glutes to raise your torso back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Glute Kickback
desc: The Glute Kickback is an isolation exercise that targets the glutes. This exercise helps a ton with improving your mind muscle connection with your glutes.
cues: Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement.
Point your toe away from your midline at the top of the movement
steps: Attach an ankle cuff to a low pulley on a cable machine.
Fasten the cuff to your ankle and face the machine, standing a short distance away for tension.
Hold onto the machine for support and maintain a slight bend in your supporting leg.
Sweep your working leg back, pointing your toe outward at the top, extending your hip until your glutes are fully contracted.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement, focusing on the contraction.
Slowly return to the starting position under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Goblet Box Squat
desc: Goblet Box Squats are great progression to bodyweight box squats. Using a box ensures that you hit the proper depth each time without risk of falling backwards.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Goblet Squat

Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Goblet Squat with Pulse

name: Hack Squat (Facing the Machine)
desc: The Hack Squat (facing machine) is an excellent squat accessory, and allows us to push close to failure with low risk of injury because of the fixed track of the hack squat.

Alternate touching your left shoulder with your right hand and your right shoulder with your left hand, keeping your hips as still as possible.
Each touch should last 2 seconds to help emphasize activating your shoulder and core stabilizers

name: Hanging Knee Raise - CM
desc: The Hanging Knee Raise is a core-strengthening exercise that primarily targets the lower abdominal muscles. It's also effective for improving grip strength and overall stability.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears
Focus on using your abs to lift your knees, rather than swinging them up.
Exhale as you raise your knees to engage the core more deeply.
Control the descent of your legs to maximize the abdominal engagement.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with a grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Start with your legs straight and feet off the ground.
Engage your core and lift your knees towards your chest.
Raise your knees as high as you can without swinging or using momentum.
Pause at the top of the movement for a moment.
Slowly lower your knees back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
desc: Hanging Leg Raises are an advanced core exercise, intensifying the focus on the entire abdominal region, particularly the lower abs. This exercise also improves grip and forearm strength.
cues: Engage your core and keep your legs straight throughout the movement.
Avoid swinging and use a controlled motion to raise and lower your legs.
Exhale as you lift your legs to activate the core muscles more effectively.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, keeping your legs straight and feet together.
Engage your core and slowly raise your legs in front of you.
Aim to bring your legs to a 90-degree angle with your torso, or as high as possible.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position without swinging.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Heel Taps (Oblique Exercise)
desc: Heel Taps are an oblique-targeting exercise that helps strengthen the abdominal muscles, with a specific emphasis on the obliques.
cues: Think about squeezing your obliques on each rep, while holding a crunch with your abs
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Place your arms by your sides with your palms facing down.
Lift your shoulders off the ground, similar to a crunch and reach one hand toward the opposite heel, tapping it gently.
Return to the starting position and repeat the movement on the other side.
Maintain a steady pace and controlled movement throughout the exercise.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Heel Taps (Stability)
desc: The Heel Touchdown is an exercise that focuses on stabilizing the hip muscles.
steps: Begin by standing on your left leg on a step with your right foot hovering slightly off the ground.
Place your hands on your hips with your fingers pointing forward to help you tell if your hips are shifting
Maintain a slight bend in your left knee and engage your core for balance.
Slowly hinge your hips backwards and "kiss" your right heel to the ground
Keep your hips level and avoid tilting to the side as you tap your heel.
Return your right foot to the hovering position next to your left ankle.
After you finish the reps on your left side, switch legs and continue

name: Heels Elevated Bodyweight Squats
desc: Heels Elevated Bodyweight Squats focus more on your quads than other squats while still working on your glutes and adductors.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Push a little more through your toes to emphasize quad activation.
Keep your knee cap pointing in the direction of your middle toe. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
steps: Stand with your heels elevated on a stable surface, shoulder-width apart. (10lb plates or 5lb dumbbells work great)
Let your knees come forward as you squat down.
When your thighs break parallel with the floor, think about squeezing your quads to come back up to the top position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Heels Elevated Counterbalance Squat
desc: The Heels Elevated Counterbalance Squat is a challenging variation works on your quads more than other versions of squats. It will also challenge your shoulders and core strength.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Keep your kneecaps pointing in the direction of your middle toes. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
SQUEEZE your quads throughout the movement.
steps: Position your heels on an elevated platform, shoulder width apart. Weight plates or small dumbbells work great.
Hold a counterbalance weight, such as a dumbbell, plate or kettlebell, in front of your body.
Initiate the movement by letting your knees come forward, lowering yourself into a squat position.
Keep your chest up and ensure your knees track in line with your toes.
Push through your full foot, biasing the balls of your feet to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Heels Elevated Goblet Squats
desc: Heels Elevated Goblet Squats focus more on your quads than other squats while still working on your glutes and adductors.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Push a little more through your toes to emphasize quad activation.
Keep your knee cap pointing in the direction of your middle toe. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
steps: Stand with your heels elevated on a stable surface, shoulder-width apart. (10lb plates or 5lb dumbbells work great)
Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell in front of your chest.
Let your knees come forward as you squat down.
When your thighs break parallel with the floor, think about squeezing your quads to come back up to the top position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: High Plank
desc: The High Plank is a great exercise for developing your isometric core strength
cues: Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels throughout the exercise.
Engage your core muscles and maintain a strong and stable shoulder position.
steps: Begin in a push-up position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your arms fully extended.
Ensure your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels, with your feet hip-width apart.
Engage your core, glutes, and leg muscles to maintain a stable and strong plank position.
Hold the plank for the desired duration, focusing on controlled breathing and maintaining proper form.

name: Hip Airplanes
desc: Hip Airplanes are a mobility and stability exercise that target the hip joint's range of motion while enhancing balance. It's like you're tilting and rotating your hips as if you're an airplane in flight.
steps: Begin by standing on one leg with your knee slightly bent.
Keep your hands on your hips for balance.
Slowly hinge your hips back, tilting your torso forward while extending your other leg straight behind you.
Continue to tilt your torso until it's parallel to the ground, creating a "T" shape with your body.
Hold this position for a few seconds.
Begin to rotate your hips open, while maintaining balance. Hold for a second before leveling your hips again (still in a "T" shape)
Tilt your hips closed, maintaining balance, then return to a levelled hip position
Return to the upright position, with your elevated foot still hovering. Repeat.

name: Hip Bridge
desc: The Bodyweight Hip Bridge is a fundamental lower body exercise that primarily targets the glutes and hamstrings. It's excellent for strengthening the posterior chain, enhancing pelvic stability, and can help improve posture and alleviate lower back pain.
cues: Press through your heels to lift your hips, keeping your toes on the ground.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement for maximal engagement.
Keep your chin slightly tucked to maintain a neutral neck and spine.
Avoid hyperextending your lower back as you lift your hips.
Engage your core throughout the movement to support your lower back.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place your arms flat on the ground alongside your body for stability.
Press your heels into the floor and lift your hips towards the ceiling by squeezing your glutes.
Lift until your knees, hips, and shoulders form a straight line.
Hold the position at the top for a moment, then slowly lower your hips back to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
subs: Single-Leg Hip Bridge (to increase the difficulty and focus on one leg at a time)

name: Hip Thrusts
desc: The Hip Thrust is one of the best exercises for developing your glutes.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach, avoid arching in your lower back.
Drive through your heels like you're trying to push them through the floor.
Pause the the top of each rep, and SQUEEZE your glutes.
steps: Sit on the ground with your upper back against a bench and a padded barbell positioned directly above your hips.
Bring your heels in so they're close to your butt, keeping your feet hip width apart.
Place your elbows on the bench, to keep your balance as you push heels into the ground to bring the bar up off the ground.
Grab the bar just outside shoulder width to balance the bar. The bench should be positioned just below your shoulder blades.
Drive your heels down, and squeeze your glutes to lift the bar as high as you can.
Slowly lower the bar back down, keeping pressure through your heels.
Lightly touch the weight plates to the ground and repeat.
Repeat.

name: Inch Worm
desc: Inchworms are a dynamic stretching exercise that targets multiple muscle groups, including the hamstrings, lower back, and shoulders. This exercise helps improve flexibility and mobility in the entire body.
steps: Begin in a standing position with your feet hip-width apart.
Keeping your legs as straight as possible, bend forward at your hips, reaching your hands toward the floor.
Walk your hands forward on the floor, keeping your legs straight or with a slight bend at the knees.
Continue walking your hands forward as far as you can while maintaining good control of your movement
Walk your hands back toward your feet, returning to the forward bend position.
Rise up to a standing position, pushing through your heels and rolling up one vertebra at a time.

name: Incline Cable Fly
desc: The Incline Cable Crossover is an effective exercise for targeting the upper chest muscles.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Pretend that you're wrapping your arms around a huge oak tree, trying to give it a hug.
steps: Adjust the pulleys to the bottom position, and set a bench to a slight incline between the pulleys.
Grasp the handles with your palms facing up and position yourself on the bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows and engage your core throughout the movement.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest, focusing on squeezing your upper chest muscles.
Hold the contraction for a moment, feeling the tension in your upper chest.
Slowly release the handles back to the starting position, feeling the stretch in your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Interval Run
desc: Zone 4.0+

name: Inverted Skull Crusher
desc: The Inverted Skull Crusher is a bodyweight exercise that primarily targets the triceps. Performed using a bar set at waist or hip height, this movement mimics the traditional skull crusher but utilizes your body weight for resistance.
cues: Keep your body straight from head to heels by engaging your core throughout the movement.
Bend only at the elbows, keeping them pointed forward to isolate the triceps.
Lower your nose toward the bar in a controlled manner without sagging your hips.
Avoid flaring your elbows out to maintain proper form and maximize triceps activation.
Exhale as you push back up, inhaling as you lower yourself toward the bar.
steps: Setup: Position a barbell securely in a squat rack or Smith machine at about waist height. Alternatively, use a fixed horizontal bar or the edge of a sturdy table or countertop.

Starting Position: Stand facing the bar and grasp it with an overhand grip (palms down), hands shoulder-width apart. Step back so your arms are fully extended, and your body forms a straight line angled toward the bar. Your feet should be together or hip-width apart for stability.
Engage Your Core: Tighten your abdominal muscles to maintain a rigid plank-like posture. Ensure your head, shoulders, hips, and ankles are aligned.

Lowering Phase: While keeping your body straight, bend your elbows to lower your nose toward the bar. Focus on moving only your forearms; your upper arms should remain stationary with elbows pointing forward. Inhale as you descend, maintaining control and avoiding any jerky movements.
Squeeze Triceps at the Bottom: Pause briefly when your nose is close to or lightly touches the bar. Ensure your elbows stay close to your body and don't flare out.
Lifting Phase: Exhale as you press through your hands to straighten your arms, pushing your body back up to the starting position. Keep your core engaged to prevent your hips from sagging or rising.
Maintain Form: Throughout the movement, keep your shoulders down and away from your ears. Avoid using momentum; the motion should be smooth and controlled.
Repeat Repetitions: Perform the desired number of repetitions, ensuring consistent form and breathing patterns.

name: Inverted Suspension Trainer Row (Bent Knee)
desc: Inverted Row (Bent Knee) The Bent Knee Inverted Row is the easiest version of the inverted row and a great starting point before you progress to the straight-leg version. Bending your knees puts your feet underneath you instead of out in front, which means you're lifting less of your own bodyweight on every rep.
cues: Pull your elbows into your back pockets, not out to the sides.
Imagine you're trying to snap the handles apart as you pull. You won't, but your upper back will fire a lot harder.
Squeeze your glutes like you're holding a full glass of water on your hips that you can't spill.
The higher you walk your feet under you, the easier it gets. Walk them out to make it harder.
steps: Set the straps so the handles hang around waist height and grip one in each hand, palms facing each other.
Walk your feet forward and sit back until your arms are straight and you're leaning back with tension in the straps.
Bend your knees to roughly 90 degrees with your feet flat on the floor, then drive your hips up so your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Pull yourself up by driving your elbows back until the handles reach your ribs.
Pause for a second at the top and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself back down slowly, letting your shoulder blades spread apart at the bottom for a full stretch.
Keep your hips up the entire set. The moment they sag, you're done.
muscles: Glutes and Core (holding your hips up)

name: Jack Knives
desc: Jack Knives are an advanced core exercise.
cues: Maintain control throughout the movement, focusing on engaging your core.
Avoid using momentum to lift your legs and upper body.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs fully extended and your arms stretched overhead.
Simultaneously lift your legs and upper body, reaching your hands towards your toes.
Pause at the top of the movement and focus on feeling the contraction in your abs.
Slowly lower your legs and upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on maintaining proper form and controlled breathing.
subs: Sit-ups + Lying Leg Raises (One After Another)

name: Jump Lunges
desc: Jump Lunges are a dynamic lower body exercise that are great for building your cardio, and plyometric strength.
cues: Maintain proper lunge form by keeping your front knee aligned with your ankle.
Explode off the ground with each jump, engaging your leg muscles.
steps: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart.
Take a step forward with your right foot, lowering your body into a lunge position.
Your right knee should be bent at a 90-degree angle, and your left knee should hover just above the ground.
Explosively push off the ground with both feet, switching the position of your legs in mid-air.
Land softly with your left foot forward and your right foot back in a lunge position.
Continue to alternate between left and right lunges with each jump.
Maintain a controlled and fluid motion, focusing on your form.
Perform the exercise for the desired number of repetitions or a specified time duration.

name: Jumping Jacks - CM
desc: Jumping Jacks are a classic cardiovascular exercise that helps improve overall fitness, coordination, and endurance.
cues: Maintain an upright posture throughout the exercise. Keep your core engaged to stabilize your body. Land softly on the balls of your feet to reduce impact on your joints. Ensure full range of motion with both arms and legs.
steps: Stand upright with your feet together and your arms at your sides. Jump up and spread your feet wider than shoulder-width apart while simultaneously raising your arms overhead to form an "X" shape. Land softly on the balls of your feet with your knees slightly bent to absorb the impact. Quickly jump back to the starting position, bringing your feet together and lowering your arms back to your sides. Repeat the jumping motion continuously for the desired duration or number of repetitions, maintaining a steady rhythm.
subs: Step Jacks (stepping out to the side instead of jumping) High Knees Mountain Climbers

name: Kettlebell Push Press
desc: The Kettlebell Push Press is a compound exercise that combines a leg drive with an overhead press. It targets the shoulders, triceps, and a little bit of legs, making it a powerful full-body movement.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Think about using your legs to pop the weights up, making a smooth transition into a shoulder press
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder height.
Bend your knees and hips slightly, preparing for the leg drive.
Explosively push through your legs, extending your knees and hips while pressing the kettlebells overhead.
Finish at the top of the movement so your wrists are directly above your shoulders.
Lower the kettlebells back to shoulder height with control.
subs: Dumbbell Seated Shoulder Press (to emphasize shoulder your shoulders)

name: Knee Pushups
desc: Knee Pushups are a modified version of traditional pushups that provide assistance to those working on their upper body strength. They primarily target the chest, shoulders, and triceps.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Think about screwing your hands into the floor, left hand screwing in counterclockwise and right hand screwing in clockwise
steps: Kneel on the ground with your knees hip-width apart.
Place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, directly under your shoulders.
Maintain a straight line from your head to your knees throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Descend until your chest is just above the ground.
Push up through your palms to return to the starting position.
Engage your core for stability throughout the exercise.

name: Knee Side Plank
desc: The Knee Side Plank is a great isometric core exercise that mostly works on your obliques and shoulder stability while also activating the outside of your glutes
cues: Maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout the exercise.
Engage your core muscles and avoid allowing your hips to sag or rotate.
steps: Lie on your side with your knees bent and one forearm supporting your upper body. Your elbow should be directly under your shoulder.
Your knees should be stacked on top of each other, and your butt should be pushed as far forward as you can. To extend through your hips.
Squeeze your obliques to raise your on top of each other and lift your hips off the ground, forming a straight line from your head to your knees.
Engage your core and hold the position for the desired duration.
Repeat the exercise on the other side.

name: Kneeling Hip CARS (Controlled Articular Rotations)
desc: Kneeling Hip CARS are a mobility exercise that targets the hip joint's range of motion and control while in a kneeling position.
steps: Begin in a kneeling position, hugging a structure to your side (a squat rack is ideal)
Maintain an upright posture with the hip closest to the squat rack as close to the rack the entire movement
Lift your outside knee backwards off the ground a few inches.
Slowly and with control, draw a circle with your outside knee, moving it outward, then upward, until it is directly in front of you, holding it as high as you can
Reverse the movement, keeping your knee as high as you can until you need to lower it to get back to the starting position
Repeat :)

name: Landmine Row
desc: The Landmine Row is a great exercise for developing your entire back. I'd recommend using 25lb plates so you can have a larger range of motion without touching the weights to your chest.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Drive through your elbows, thinking of your hands as hooks
steps: Secure one end of the barbell into the landmine attachment or corner.
Stand with the bar in between your legs, with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Hook a v-bar attachment underneath the bar, so it's secured just below the weights.
Maintain a straight back and pull the V-Bar towards your lower chest, leading with your elbows and focusing on engaging your back muscles.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the peak of the movement.
Control the V-Bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Landmine Single Shoulder Press
desc: The Kneeling Landmine Single Arm Shoulder Press is an effective exercise that targets the shoulder muscles without needing a ton of overhead mobility
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
steps: Set up the landmine in front of you and load the appropriate weight.
Kneel down in front of the landmine, ensuring your back is straight and your core is engaged.
Grip the landmine with one hand, positioning it at shoulder height.
Press the landmine upward, fully extending your arm while maintaining control and stability.
Slowly lower the landmine back to shoulder height, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions on each arm.

name: Lateral Leg Swing
desc: Lateral Leg Swings are a dynamic stretching exercise that targets the hip abductors and adductors, promoting flexibility and mobility in the hips and thighs.
steps: Stand next to a sturdy support, like a wall or railing, for balance.
Hold onto the support with one hand and keep your core engaged.
Begin by standing tall with your feet together.
Swing one leg out to the side as far as comfortably possible.
Keep the leg straight or with a slight bend at the knee.
Swing the leg back toward the midline of your body, crossing it in front of your standing leg.
Continue to swing your leg back and forth in a controlled motion.

name: Leg Extensions
desc: Leg Extensions are a quad BURNER. Try to focus on getting a good squeeze through your quads rather than trying to move heavy weight
cues: Squeeze your quads at the top of the movement.
Think about pulling your butt into the seat while pointing your toes up towards your face.
steps: Sit on the leg extension machine with your back flat against the seat and your legs positioned under the pads. The pad should be just above your ankles.
Extend your legs upward, focusing on squeezing your quadriceps at the peak of the movement.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position. Avoid letting the weight all the way down to maintain tension in your quads.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Leg Press
desc: The leg press is a powerful lower body exercise that primarily targets your quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. It's a great way to build strength and muscle in your legs.
steps: Begin by sitting on the leg press machine with your back flat, and your butt all the way in the corner
Place your feet about shoulder width apart with your toes slightly pointing out
Push evenly through your full foot
****DON'T LOCK YOUR KNEES COMPLETELY OUT (you'd most likely be fine, but leave a soft bend in your knees to be safe)
lower the weight slowly, making sure your knees caps point in the same direction as your toes (knees not caving in)

name: Leg Press (Plate Loaded MP)
desc: The leg press is a powerful lower body exercise that primarily targets your quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. It's a great way to build strength and muscle in your legs. Input the weight as the TOTAL weight of the plates plus the weight of the machine. If you don't know the weight of the machine, only put in the total weight of the plates.
steps: Begin by sitting on the leg press machine with your back flat, and your butt all the way in the corner
Place your feet about shoulder width apart with your toes slightly pointing out
Push evenly through your full foot
****DON'T LOCK YOUR KNEES COMPLETELY OUT (you'd most likely be fine, but leave a soft bend in your knees to be safe)
lower the weight slowly, making sure your knees caps point in the same direction as your toes (knees not caving in)

name: Lizard with Rotation
desc: The Lizard with Rotation is a dynamic yoga-inspired stretch that targets your hip flexors, groin, and thoracic spine. This movement combines a deep hip opener with a spinal twist, promoting flexibility and mobility.
steps: Start in a runner's lunge with your front finger tips in line with your toes
Keep your back leg straight and active, pushing through your heel to feel a stretch in your hip flexor.
Focus on getting a good rotation in your mid back as your reach for the inside of your front foot with your elbow, and then reach up for the ceiling
subs: Deep Squat Stretch + Thread The Needle

name: Long Slow Run
desc: Max zone 2.9 - Below race pace

name: Low to High Cable Fly
desc: The Low to High Cable Crossover is a chest isolation exercise that focuses more on the upper fibers of your pecs.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Think about wrapping your arms around a huge oak tree.
steps: Set the pulleys to the lowest position and stand in the center of the cable machine.
Grasp the handles with your palms facing up and take a step forward in a split stance so there's tension in the cables.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows and engage your core throughout the movement.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest, focusing on squeezing your chest muscles.
Hold the contraction for a moment, feeling the tension in your chest.
Slowly release the handles back to the starting position, feeling the stretch in your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Lying Hip CARS (Controlled Articular Rotations)
desc: Lying Hip CARS are an exercise that focuses on improving hip joint mobility and control. It's like drawing circles with your hip while lying prone.
steps: Lie prone with your legs extended.
Keep your arms relaxed under your forehead.
Lift your right leg a few inches off the ground.

Begin by slowly drawing a circle as large as you can with your right knee, moving it outward, then upward. Once you reach the limit of your range of motion, return your leg to the start position and repeat.

name: Lying Leg Curl - CM
desc: The Lying Leg Curl is a great machine for developing your hamstrings.
cues: Drive up through your heels, trying to touch the pad to the back of your legs on each rep
Keep your hips pressed firmly into the bench throughout the exercise.
steps: Lie face down on the leg curl machine with your legs straight and your heels positioned under the padded lever.
Grasp the handles or sides of the machine for stability.
Exhale as you curl your legs upward, focusing on engaging your hamstrings.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower your legs back to the starting position.
Maintain a controlled motion throughout the exercise.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Lying Leg Raise
desc: The Lying Leg Raise is one of my favourite exercises for developing your abs. Most people will tell you that it focuses mostly on your lower abs, but whether you can target specific areas of your abs is contentious.
cues: Maintain control and avoid using too much momentum during the exercise.
Think about squeezing your abs to bring your legs up.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs fully extended and your hands placed under your butt.
Slowly raise your legs off the ground, keeping them straight and together.
Lift your legs until they form a 90-degree angle with your torso or as high as you can without straining your lower back.
Lower your legs back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on maintaining proper form and controlled breathing.
subs: Hanging Leg Raise (or Hanging Knee Raises)

name: Lying Leg Raise to Reverse Crunch
desc: The Lying Leg Raise to Reverse Crunch is a more advanced version of the lying leg raise.
cues: Maintain control and avoid using too much momentum during the exercise.
Think about squeezing your abs to bring your legs up.
SLOWLY uncurl your lower back onto the ground vertebrae by vertebrae
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs fully extended and your hands placed under your butt.
Slowly raise your legs off the ground, keeping them straight and together.
Lift your legs until they form a 90-degree angle.
Reach your legs up towards the ceiling so your lower back comes up off the ground
Slowly uncurl your spine back onto the ground while keeping your legs pointed up
Lower your legs back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on maintaining proper form and controlled breathing.
subs: Hanging Leg Raise (or Hanging Knee Raises)

name: Machine Ab Crunch
desc: The Machine Ab Crunch is a popular gym exercise aimed at targeting the abdominal muscles. It allows for a focused movement that specifically engages the core, making it an effective option for strengthening and building the abs.
cues: Exhale and contract your abs fully at the peak of the crunch.
Keep your neck and shoulders relaxed; avoid pulling with your hands.
Imagine you're trying to shorten the distance between your ribs and hips.
steps: Sit down on the machine and secure your feet as per the machine instructions.
Grasp the handles above your head without straining your neck.
Start with your upper body slightly reclined, then contract your abdominal muscles to curl your upper body forward.
Pause at the peak of the movement, ensuring your abs are fully engaged.
Slowly return to the starting position without letting the weights rest completely between reps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Abductors
desc: Seated Abductors are great for targeting the outsides of your glutes.
cues: Push out through your knees, focusing on squeezing your glutes
steps: Sit on the machine with your legs positioned on the pads and your knees at a comfortable angle.
Press your legs outward, away from your body, feeling the activation in your outer glutes and thighs.
Maintain a neutral spine and avoid leaning during the exercise.
Slowly bring your legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Adductors
desc: Machine Adductors are an effective exercise for targeting the inner thighs , emphasizing controlled movements to activate the adductor muscles.
cues: Think about SQUEEZING your inner thighs as you bring the pads to touch
steps: Sit on the machine with your legs positioned on the pads and your knees at a comfortable angle.
Press your legs inward, towards one another, feeling the activation in your inner thighs.
Slowly bring your legs back to the starting position, feeling the stretch in your adductor muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Assisted Chin-Up
desc: ***BE MINDFUL THAT THE LOWER WEIGHT YOU SELECT, THE HARDER THE MOVEMENT WILL BE SINCE IT'S A COUNTERWEIGHT TO YOUR BODYWEIGHT Machine assisted chin-ups are an excellent exercise for building upper body strength, especially targeting the back and biceps.
steps: Set the machine to an appropriate assistance level for your strength
Start with arms fully extended engage your back as you pull yourself up
Control your descent to the starting position.
subs: Negative Chin-ups (Using a step to assist only on the way up) ***Also do fewer negative chin-ups (~3-5) if this is the substitution you choose

name: Machine Assisted Dips
desc: ***BE MINDFUL THAT THE LOWER WEIGHT YOU SELECT, THE HARDER THE MOVEMENT WILL BE SINCE IT'S A COUNTERWEIGHT TO YOUR BODYWEIGHT Machine assisted dips are a great way to target your chest, triceps, and shoulders while building upper body strength.
steps: Adjust the machine to a suitable assistance level for your strength
Start with arms fully extended and lower your body by bending your elbows
Keep your chest up and shoulders down as you push back up.

name: Machine Assisted Pull-Ups
desc: ***BE MINDFUL THAT THE LOWER WEIGHT YOU SELECT, THE HARDER THE MOVEMENT WILL BE SINCE IT'S A COUNTERWEIGHT TO YOUR BODYWEIGHT Machine assisted pull-ups are an excellent exercise for building upper body strength, especially targeting the outer fibers of your back, giving your waist a smaller appearance.
steps: Set the machine to an appropriate assistance level for your strength
Start with arms fully extended engage your back as you pull yourself up
Control your descent to the starting position.
subs: Negative Pull-ups-ups (Using a step to assist only on the way up) ***Also do fewer negative pull-ups (~3-5) if this is the substitution you choose

name: Machine Bench Press
desc: The Machine Bench Press is an effective exercise for targeting the chest muscles, emphasizing overall upper body strength and muscle development.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
steps: Adjust the machine so the handles are in line with your lower chest. Your back should be flat against the pad and your feet planted firmly on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, ensuring your arms are in line with your chest.
Press the handles upward in a controlled motion, avoiding locking your elbows out at the top.
Squeeze your chest at the end of the movement, maintaining tension in your chest muscles.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position, feeling the stretch in your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Bicep Curl
desc: Machine Bicep Curls are great for challenging your biceps in a lengthened position.
cues: Keep your upper arms and back firmly against the pads.
Focus on squeezing the biceps at the top of the movement.
Control the weight during both the lifting and lowering phases.
Avoid using momentum; let your biceps do the work.
steps: Adjust the seat and arm pad of the machine to fit your height.
Sit down and place your upper arms against the pads.
Grip the handles with palms facing up.
Curl the handles towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Chest Press
desc: The Machine Chest Press is an effective exercise for targeting the chest muscles, emphasizing overall upper body strength and muscle development.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
steps: Adjust the seat and handles so the handles are in line with your lower chest. Your back should be flat against the pad and your feet planted firmly on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, ensuring your arms are in line with your chest.
Press the handles forward in a controlled motion, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Squeeze your chest at the end of the movement, maintaining tension in your chest muscles.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position, feeling the stretch in your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Glute Kickback
desc: The Machine Glute Kickback is an effective exercise targeting the gluteal muscles, especially the gluteus maximus.
cues: Press through your heel as you extend your leg back to maximize glute engagement.
Squeeze your glutes at the peak of the movement
Avoid arching your lower back; the movement should come from your hip extension.
steps: Adjust the Machine: Set the pad or footplate of the Glute Kickback Machine to align with the back of your working leg’s ankle or foot.
Starting Position: Stand facing the machine, supporting yourself by holding onto the machine’s handles or support bars for balance.
Position Your Foot: Place the working leg’s foot securely on the machine’s footplate or against the pad.
Engage Your Core: Keep your abdominal muscles tight to stabilize your spine and pelvis.
Slight Knee Bend: Maintain a slight bend in the standing (supporting) leg to reduce strain and enhance balance.
Execute the Kickback: Press your working leg straight back in a controlled motion by extending at the hip. Focus on pushing through your heel.
Squeeze at the Top: At full extension, squeeze your glute muscle firmly without arching your back or overextending.
Controlled Return: Slowly bring your leg back to the starting position, resisting the weight to maintain tension on the muscle.
Avoid Resting: Do not let the weight stack touch down completely between repetitions to keep continuous tension.
Repeat Repetitions: Complete the desired number of reps on one leg before switching to the other leg.

name: Machine Hip Thrust
desc: This is a great alternative to barbell hip thrusts that requires practically no setup.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach, avoid arching in your lower back.
Drive through your heels like you're trying to push them through the platform.
Pause the the top of each rep, and SQUEEZE your glutes.
steps: Load the machine with an appropriate weight (start light if you've never tried these)
Lay on the pad, on follow the instructions on the machine to secure the belt in a comfortable position across your hips.
Drive your heels down to lift the weights, and adjust the safeties so you can access a full range of motion
Slowly lower the weights down as low as you comfortably can.
Drive your heels down, and squeeze your glutes to lift the weights as high as you can.
Repeat.

name: Machine Lateral Raise
desc: The Machine Lateral Raise is a great shoulder developing exercise with minimal injury risk.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Drive up through your elbows
steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself in the machine as it instructs.
Grab the handles and use your elbows and forearms to drive the pads up.
Pause at the top of the movement, feeling the contraction in your shoulders.
Lower the pads back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Leg Press
desc: The Machine Leg Press is a popular strength-training exercise that targets the lower body, specifically the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes.
cues: Brace your core for the entire movement
Keep your knees in line with your middle toe. They shouldn't be too far out, or cave into the midline.
Push evenly through your full foot. You can think about trying to push your feet "through the platform"
steps: Adjust the machine so you get the largest range of motion possible without sacrificing your form
Sit on the machine and position yourself so that your butt is in the corner of the seat.

Place your feet flat against the footplate. *Shoulder width with your toes slightly pointed out is best for most people. The higher up your feet are the more hamstring and glutes you work, the lower your feet are the more quads you work.
Grasp the side handles for stability.
Press the platform away by extending your legs, exhaling as you push.
Once your legs are almost fully extended (avoid locking your knees), pause briefly.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position by bending your knees, inhaling as you do so.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Rear Delt Row
desc: The Machine Rear Delt Row is a strength exercise that targets the posterior deltoids (rear deltoids) in the shoulders, along with the upper back muscles.
cues: Keep your spine straight and chest up throughout the exercise.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the peak of the movement.
Control the movement both when pulling and returning to the starting position.
steps: Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad.
Grasp the handles with your arms extended in front of you.
Pull the handles back towards your torso, keeping your elbows high.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Row
desc: Machine Rows are a great way to target your entire back. Sit at the machine with your chest against the pad and grasp the handles with a neutral grip. Drive your elbows backwards while squeezing your shoulder blades together, then slowly return to the starting position.
steps: Adjust the seat and handles so your arms are fully extended when you start.
Maintain a straight back and avoid using momentum to pull the weight.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for the entire movement.
Control the weight as you return to the starting position.
muscles: Back (Lats, rhomboids and mid and lower trapezius)
Rear Shoulders (Posterior Deltoids) Cues (Choose 1 or 2 to focus on at one time)
Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Drive through your elbows, thinking of your hands as hooks

name: Machine Shoulder Press
desc: The Machine Shoulder Press is a great exercise for targeting the shoulders while keeping injury risk low.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
steps: Adjust the seat and handles to the appropriate position and sit with your back flat against the seat.
Grasp the handles with a neutral grip and push the handles upward, extending your arms fully.
Avoid arching your back and maintain a stable base.
Lower the handles back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Tricep Extension
desc: The Machine Tricep Extension is a great exercise that I often include near the end of a workout since you can push very close to failure without risk of an injury.
cues: Keep your elbows in line with the machine's "pivot point"
Control the movement both when extending and returning.
Focus on squeezing the triceps at the end of each extension.
steps: Sit down and grip the handles, palms facing down.
Slide your elbows down the pad until they are aligned with the machine's pivot point.
Keeping your elbows stationary, extend your arms fully.
Slowly return to the starting position, avoiding letting the weight stack rest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Machine Tricep Press
desc: Machine Tricep Press - Machine Dip The Machine Tricep Press - often called the Machine Dip - is a compound pushing movement that primarily targets the triceps while also training the chest and shoulders. It’s a great way to overload the triceps safely without needing to support your full bodyweight.
cues: Keep your chest tall and shoulders down
Drive through your palms, not your shoulders
Elbows track slightly back - not flared wide
Control the negative - do not bounce at the bottom
Lock out strong without shrugging
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at mid-chest level when seated.
Sit tall with your back supported and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the handles firmly and pull your shoulders down and back.
Press the handles downward by extending your elbows.
Keep your torso steady and avoid leaning excessively forward.
Press until your arms are fully extended but not hyperextended.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position under control.
Repeat for the prescribed number of reps.

name: Mountain Climbers - CM
desc: Mountain Climbers are a dynamic full-body exercise that mostly targets the core, but you'll also get shoulder stability and cardiovascular benefits from doing them.
cues: Squeeze your core like you're going to be poked in the stomach the entire time
steps: Begin in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line.
Drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs, as if you're running in place.
Maintain a rapid and controlled pace, focusing on proper form and breathing.
Continue the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.

name: Negative Chin-Ups
desc: Negative Chin-Ups are a great exercise for building chin-up strength. It focuses exclusively on the negative portion of a chin-up.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
SQUEEZE your abs and glutes to avoid swinging
steps: Grab a pull-up bar at shoulder width with an underhand grip.
Jump or use a step to get your chin over the bar and SLOWLY lower yourself down
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears, maintaining a proud chest
Aim for a slow and controlled descent, ideally taking a count of 3-5 seconds.
Once your arms are fully extended, jump or step up to raise your chin above the bar again and repeat.

name: Negative Pull-Ups
desc: Negative Pull-Ups are a great exercise for building Pull-up strength. It focuses exclusively on the negative portion of a pull-up.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
SQUEEZE your abs and glutes to avoid swinging
steps: Grab a pull-up bar at shoulder width with an overhand grip.
Jump or use a step to get your chin over the bar and SLOWLY lower yourself down
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears, maintaining a proud chest
Aim for a slow and controlled descent, ideally taking a count of 3-5 seconds.
Once your arms are fully extended, jump or step up to raise your chin above the bar again and repeat.

name: Outdoor Cardio
desc: Any cardio works great here: running, walking, tennis, etc. Don't push yourself too hard here, it's meant as a recovery.

name: Overhead Band Tricep Extension
desc: The Overhead Band Tricep Extension is are especially effective for targeting the long head of your triceps. Major Areas Worked
cues: Extend your arms fully at the top of the movement.
Keep your elbows high throughout the movement
steps: Attach a cable to a medium-high anchor point (somewhere around head height)
Grasp the cable with both hands and turn away from the anchor, elbows bent and hands near your head.
Step forward into a staggered stance for stability.
Extend your arms fully above your head.
Slowly return to the starting position, allowing your forearms to move towards your biceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Overhead Cable Tricep Extension
desc: The Overhead Cable Tricep Extension is are especially effective for targeting the long head of your triceps.
cues: Extend your arms fully at the top of the movement.
Keep your elbows high throughout the movement
steps: Attach a rope to a low pulley on a cable machine
Grasp the rope with both hands and turn away from the machine, elbows bent and hands near your head.
Step forward into a staggered stance for stability.
Extend your arms fully above your head, pulling the rope apart at the end of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, allowing your forearms to move towards your biceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Overhead Carry
desc: The Overhead Carry is an excellent exercise for building shoulder strength, and stability.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Keep your core engaged and maintain a straight posture.
Start walking forward with controlled steps, keeping the dumbbells overhead.
Avoid arching your lower back or shrugging your shoulders.
Continue walking for a designated distance or time.
When finished, safely lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height.

name: Overhead Rope Tricep Extension* duplicate exercise
Pec Deck
desc: The Pec Deck is an isolation exercise that targets the chest muscles.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Squeeze the handles together in the middle
Imagine you're trying to hug a huge oak tree
steps: Sit with your back supported against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with your arms nearly straight (there should be a micro bend in your elbows_
Bring the handles together in front of your chest, focusing on squeezing your chest muscles.
Hold the contraction for a moment, feeling the tension in your chest.
Slowly release the handles back to the starting position, feeling the stretch in your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Physio Ball Crunches
desc: The Physio Ball Crunch intensifies the activation of the abdominal muscles compared to traditional floor crunches by increasing the range of motion and engaging stabilizer muscles. It’s excellent for developing core strength, improving balance, and enhancing overall posture.
cues: Exhale as you crunch up, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Think about "curling your spine up" trying to touch the bottom of your ribs to your pelvis
steps: Starting Position: Sit on the physioball with your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Walk Forward: Slowly walk your feet forward, allowing the ball to roll under you until it supports your lower to mid-back. Your thighs and torso should form a straight line parallel to the floor.
Hand Placement: Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands lightly behind your head without pulling on your neck.
Engage Core Muscles: Tighten your abdominal muscles by drawing your belly button inward.
Perform the Crunch: Lift your upper body by contracting your abs, curling your ribcage toward your pelvis.
Pause at the Top: Hold the contraction for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your abdominal muscles.
Lower with Control: Slowly return to the starting position, keeping tension in your abs and maintaining balance on the ball.
Repeat Repetitions: Perform the desired number of repetitions, ensuring consistent form throughout.
muscles: Stabilizing Muscles (including lower back and glutes)
subs: Traditional Floor Crunch: A basic crunch performed on the floor without equipment.
Decline Bench Sit-Up: Increases difficulty by adding an incline to target the abs more intensely.
Plank Variations: Such as forearm planks or side planks to engage the core isometrically.

name: Pike Pushups
desc: Pike Pushups are a bodyweight shoulder exercise that targets the deltoid muscles and help build shoulder strength and stability. This exercise resembles an inverted "V" shape.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Think about screwing your hands into the floor, left hand screwing in counterclockwise and right hand screwing in clockwise
steps: Start in a plank position with your hands a little wider than shoulder-width apart and your hips raised, forming an inverted "V" shape with your body. (similar to a downward facing dog)
Lower your head toward the ground by bending your elbows.
Push up through your shoulders to return to the starting position.
Engage your core for stability throughout the exercise.

name: Plank - CM
desc: The Plank is a fundamental core exercise. Top tier.
cues: Squeeze your midsection like you're about to be poked in the stomach.
Avoid sticking your butt in the air, or letting your lower back slouch.
steps: Support yourself on your elbows and toes, making sure your elbows are directly underneath your shoulders.
Engage your core muscles, glutes, and quads to maintain the position. Your body should be in a straight line from your heels through the top of your head.

name: Pronated Lat Pulldown
desc: The Pronated Lat Pulldown are great for developing your back which helps give the illusion of a smaller waist
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Drive through your elbows, thinking of your hands as hooks
steps: Sit on the Lat Pulldown machine with your knees secured under the pads and your hands on the bar using an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Maintain a slight arch in your lower back and keep your chest up throughout the movement.
Pull the bar down towards your collarbone, focusing on engaging your back muscles.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom of the movement.
Control the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Prone Cobra
desc: The Prone Cobra is a back-strengthening exercise that targets the muscles of the upper back. It promotes improved posture and back strength.
cues: Pull your shoulder blades back and down as if you're trying to pinch a pencil between them.
Think about sticking your chest out at the top of each rep
steps: Lie face down on a mat or the floor with your arms extended straight out to the sides, palms facing down.
Keep your legs extended and toes pointing down.
Engage your core muscles for stability.
Begin by gently lifting your chest and arms off the ground, squeezing your shoulder blades together, and bringing your arms slightly down towards your feet
Avoid using your neck muscles; focus on using your upper back.
Hold this lifted position for 2-3 seconds while squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower your chest and arms back down to the ground.
Repeat

name: Prone Scorpions
desc: Prone Scorpions are like a stretchy dance move for your lower back, and hips.
steps: Start by lying face down on the floor, arms out wide like you're ready to give someone a big hug.
Lift your right foot and bend your right knee, swinging it over to the left side, trying to reach up for your hand
Go back to the starting position and switch sides

name: Pull-Ups
desc: Pull-ups are great for developing your back which helps give the illusion of a smaller waist
cues: Keeping your shoulders down away from your ears
Squeezing your back as you drive down through your elbows
Lowering yourself under control

name: Pulse Squats
desc: Pulse Squats are a progression to regular squats and can build a ton of lactic acid in your legs. Get ready for a good burn!
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Keep an even center of pressure across the “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Keep your knee cap pointing in the direction of your middle toe. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
Screw your feet into the floor, left foot screwing in counterclockwise and right foot screwing in clockwise
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart or slightly wider, maintaining a neutral spine and engaged core.
Open up through your hips, dropping your butt down towards your heels.
At the bottom of the rep, perform a small pulse before squatting all the way back up to the top position.
Repeat for the prescribed number of reps.

name: Push-Ups
desc: Push-ups are a classic bodyweight exercise that builds strength in your chest, shoulders, and triceps while also engaging your core for stability. It's a simple yet effective move that can be done anywhere.
steps: Begin of the floor with your entire body tense
Place your hands shoulder width apart, your thumbs should be just below your armpits, with your fingers pointing forward
Keeping your elbows at a ~45 degree angle from your body, push you your hands to the top position
Lower yourself down with control

name: Quad Foam Roll
desc: The Quad Foam Roll is a self-myofascial release (SMR) technique that helps relieve muscle tension and improve mobility in the quadriceps (front thigh muscles). It's an excellent exercise to reduce muscle tightness and soreness.
steps: Begin by laying prone with a foam roller directly under one or both of your quads
Come into a plank on your elbows, leaving your quad(s) relaxed
Try to find tender spots in your quads with the foam roller
Once you find a tender spot, try to add pressure to the area using the foam roller while leaving your muscle relaxed
Spend 5-10 seconds relaxing into the position, then make very small movements over the tender spot for 5-10 seconds
Find another tender spot, and repeat
For bonus points, you can try bringing your heel to touch your butt while the foam roller is in a tender spot

name: Rack Pull - CM
desc: The Barbell Rack Pull isolates the top part of a conventional deadlift. It's great for developing your posterior chain, and grip strength.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Keep an even center of pressure across the “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Screw your feet into the floor, left foot screwing in counterclockwise and right foot screwing in clockwise
“Spread the floor” (you can imagine standing on wet newspaper that you’re trying to split down the middle)
Think about trying to snap the bar like a piece of spaghetti
steps: Position a barbell at knee height on a rack or an elevated platform.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and grip the barbell with an overhand grip.
Hinge at your hips and slightly bend your knees, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Pull the barbell upward, focusing on squeezing your glutes and hamstrings at the top of the movement.
Lower the barbell back down to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Recovery Run
desc: Super slow

name: Reverse Crunch
desc: The Reverse Crunch is a great low impact exercise that is phenomenal to help you develop a better mind muscle connection with your abs
cues: Exhale as you bring your knees in, and SQUEEZE your abs
Slowly uncoil your vertebrae down onto the ground as you come down
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs bent and your feet flat on the ground.
Place your hands by your sides or underneath your glutes for support.
Engage your core and lift your legs, bringing your knees towards your chest.
At the top of the movement, focus on contracting your lower abs and lifting your hips off the ground.
Lower your legs back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on maintaining proper form and controlled breathing.

name: Reverse Curl
desc: The Barbell Reverse Curl is great for developing your forearms, while also hitting your biceps.
cues: Keep your wrists straight throughout the exercise.
Keep your elbows glued to your sides.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip. Keep your thumbs on top of the bar.
Keep your elbows close to your body and your wrists straight.
Curl the barbell up towards your chest, contracting your forearm muscles.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.

name: Reverse Pec Deck
desc: The Reverse Pec Deck is an isolation exercise that targets the muscles of the posterior shoulder, which is great for your posture and physique!
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Keep a SLIGHT bend in your elbows the entire time (your arms should be nearly straight)
