steps: Adjust the seat and handles to your appropriate height and sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down, and ensure your arms are parallel to the floor.
Maintain a neutral spine and engage your core throughout the movement.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and bring your arms back until they are in line with your body.
Feel the contraction in your rear delts and upper back.
Control the handles back to the starting position, maintaining tension in your rear delts.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Rice Bucket
desc: Great exercise to work out every tiny muscle in your hands and forearms! Take rests as needed

name: Rolling Lizard
desc: The Rolling Lizard Stretch is a dynamic stretching exercise that targets the hip flexors, and groin. This exercise helps improve hip mobility and flexibility in the lower body.
steps: Begin in a runner's lunge with opposite fingers and toes in line with each other
Push back through your back heel to feel a stretch across your back hip flexor
Place your free hand on top of your knee, and trace large circles to feel a stretch through your inner thigh
Make sure you keep your front foot firmly rooted into the ground while going through the movement

name: Romanian Deadlift
desc: The Romanian Deadlifts are an effective compound exercise that targets the posterior chain, emphasizing controlled hip hinging movements with a barbell or dumbbells. This exercise helps build hamstring and glute strength, promoting improved hip mobility and stability.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Screw your feet into the floor, left foot screwing in counterclockwise and right foot screwing in clockwise
Squeeze your glutes like you're trying to crush a walnut
Think about trying to snap the bar like a piece of spaghetti
Reach up and back with your hips like you’re trying to close a door behind you with your butt
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, grabbing a barbell at shoulder width like you're trying to snap it in hallf.
Hinge at your hips and push your glutes backward, feeling the stretch in your hamstrings.
Lower the weight as far as comfortably possible while maintaining a neutral spine.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to return to the starting position, focusing on squeezing your glutes at the top.
Avoid rounding your back and maintain control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Rowing Machine
desc: Rowing Machine is a full-body conditioning exercise that builds aerobic capacity, leg drive, and upper-body pulling strength while being very joint-friendly.
subs: SkiErg Any other kind or cardio machine (bike, elliptical, treadmill)

name: Run The Rack Bicep Curls
desc: Input "weight" as the first weight you select. Run The Rack Bicep Curls is an advanced bicep exercise that involves performing bicep curls with progressively lighter dumbbells without rest, starting with the heaviest weights and gradually moving down to lighter ones.
cues: SQUEEZE your hands and biceps throughout your curls
Keep tension in your biceps by keeping a slight bend in your elbows at the bottom of the movement
steps: Start with the heaviest set of dumbbells you can handle and perform 5-6 curls with, ensuring proper form and control throughout the movement.
Once you reach muscle fatigue with the heaviest weight, switch to the next lighter set of dumbbells without taking any rest.
Continue the pattern, gradually decreasing the weight until you reach 10lb dumbbells or whatever feels appropriate for you.
Focus on maintaining proper form and control even as you decrease the weight.

name: Run The Rack Lateral Raise
desc: Input "weight" as the first weight you select. Run The Rack Lateral Raises are an advanced shoulder exercise that involves performing lateral raises with progressively lighter dumbbells without rest, starting with the heaviest weights and gradually moving down to lighter ones.
cues: Imagine you're trying to pour 2 pitchers of water out to the sides
Lead with your elbows
steps: Start with the heaviest set of dumbbells you can handle and perform 5-6 raises with, ensuring proper form and control throughout the movement.
Once you reach muscle fatigue with the heaviest weight, switch to the next lighter set of dumbbells without taking any rest.
Continue the pattern, gradually decreasing the weight until you reach 5lb dumbbells or whatever feels appropriate for you.
Focus on maintaining proper form and control even as you decrease the weight.

name: Russian Twists
desc: Russian Twists are a classic core exercise that mainly targets the obliques. If you feel pain in your lower back while doing these, try them with your feet on the ground
cues: Control the movement and avoid using momentum to twist your torso.
steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and lift your feet to hover off the ground
Lean back slightly to engage your core and maintain a stable posture.
Hold a weight or medicine ball in front of your chest or clasp your hands together.
Twist your torso from side to side, bringing the weight or your hands towards the floor on each side.
Control the movement and focus on feeling the contraction in your obliques.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form and controlled breathing.

name: Scapular Circles
desc: Scapular Circles are one of my favourite shoulder stability drills!
steps: Begin standing against a wall at a 45 degree angle with one shoulder blade touching the wall
Extend the arm who's shoulder blade is touching the wall straight in front of you
Keeping your elbow locked, slowly trace the largest circle you can with your shoulder blade

name: Scapular Pushups
desc: Scapular Pushups Description: Scapular Pushups are a shoulder stability exercise that focuses on movement of the shoulder blades rather than the arms. They help improve scapular control and strengthen the muscles that support healthy shoulder function.
cues: Keep your arms straight the entire time.
Let your chest sink slightly by bringing your shoulder blades together.
Push the floor away to spread your shoulder blades apart.
Keep your core tight and body in a straight line.
steps: Start in a high plank position with hands under shoulders and arms straight.
Keep your elbows locked and core engaged.
Slowly let your chest drop slightly by retracting your shoulder blades.
Reverse the motion by pushing through your hands and protracting your shoulder blades.
Move through a small, controlled range without bending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Scissor Kicks - CM
desc: Scissor Kicks are an effective core exercise that targets the entire abdominal area, with an emphasis on the lower abs.
cues: Engage your core throughout the entire movement.
Control the motion, focusing on maintaining a steady and controlled pace.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs fully extended and your arms by your sides or underneath your glutes for support.
Engage your core and lift your legs a few inches off the ground.
Begin the movement by crossing one leg over the other, alternating the position of your legs in a scissoring motion.
Focus on feeling the contraction in your lower abs and maintaining control throughout the exercise.
Continue the scissoring motion for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on maintaining proper form and controlled breathing.

name: Seated Cable Row - CM
desc: The Cable Row is a fundamental exercise that targets the back muscles, including the lats and rhomboids. This exercise is effective for building upper body strength and enhancing overall back development.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Drive through your elbows, thinking of your hands as hooks
steps: Sit on the cable row machine and grasp the handle with a neutral grip, sitting up tall with your knees slightly bent.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the movement.
Pull the handle towards your abdomen, leading with your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Maintain a stable posture without leaning back excessively.
Control the handle back to the starting position, extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Seated Glute Stretch
desc: The Seated Glute Stretch is a simple but effective stretch that helps to alleviate tension and improve flexibility in the glutes (buttocks) and lower back.
steps: Begin by sitting with your legs extended straight out in front of you.
Bend your right knee and cross your right ankle over your left thigh, creating a figure-four shape with your legs.
Keeping your back straight, gently lean forward from your hips, reaching toward your left foot.
You should feel a stretch in your right glute and lower back.
You can "scan" your shoulders from left to right to see where you feel the biggest stretch, and then continue to stretch in that direction

name: Seated Leg Curl
desc: The Seated Leg Curl is a GREAT machine for developing your hamstrings. It has an even better reputation than lying leg curls, but both have a place in your program.
cues: Drive down through your heels.
Lean slightly forward to get a better stretch in your hamstrings when you extend your legs.
steps: Sit on the leg curl machine with your legs positioned between the top pad and bottom pad. Make sure you adjust the top pad so it's tight to the top of your legs.
Grasp the handles or sides of the machine for stability.
Exhale as you curl your legs toward your glutes, focusing on engaging your hamstrings.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then inhale as you slowly extend your legs back to the starting position.
Control the movement throughout the exercise.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Short Foot
desc: The Short Foot Exercise is a great movement for improving foot and ankle stability.
steps: Begin by standing with your feet flat on the ground.
Lift one foot slightly off the ground
Slightly raise the arch of your planted foot. A weird but effective cue I've found is imagine you're trying to pick up a marble in the arch of your foot.
With your hovering foot, reach as far to your side as you can and "kiss" your toe to the ground
Bring your hovering foot back to your center position but DON'T touch down
Reach out with your hovering foot again, but further back. Come back to the center position and repeat until you're reaching straight backwards with the hovering foot.

name: Shoulder Dislocates
desc: Shoulder dislocates are a mobility exercise that enhances shoulder flexibility and mobility. This exercise involves moving a resistance band or a stick overhead in a circular motion.
steps: Hold a resistance band or a stick with a wide grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Start with the band or stick in front of you at waist height.
Keeping your arms straight, raise the band or stick up and over your head and behind your back.
Move slowly to feel a big stretch in your chest and shoulders
Continue to bring it down in front of you until you return to the starting position.
Maintain a controlled and smooth pace throughout the movement.

name: Shoulder Touches
desc: Terrific shoulder stabilizer! Widen your stance to make it easier, and vice versa :)
cues: Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Keep your core engaged.
Avoid twisting your hips.
steps: Start in a pushup position with your hands on an elevated surface, such as a bench or step.
Maintain a straight line from your head to your tailbone, engaging your core for stability.
Alternate touching your left shoulder with your right hand and your right shoulder with your left hand, keeping your hips as still as possible.
Each touch should last 2 seconds to help emphasize activating your shoulder and core stabilizers

name: Side Lunges
desc: Side Lunges are effective lower body exercises that target the inner and outer thighs, and glutes. This exercise helps improve lower body strength, flexibility, and mobility, making it an excellent addition to any leg workout routine.
cues: Keep your chest up and your back straight throughout the movement.
Push your knees out so your kneecaps pointing in the direction of your middle toes.
Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach.
Think about squeezing your glutes and quads as you come back up to center.
steps: Stand with your feet well wider than shoulder-width apart with your toes pointed out at about 45-degrees. Option to hold a dumbbell or kettlebell to your chest.
Shift your weight to one side, while pushing your hips back, ensuring your feet remain planted and your kneecap is pointing in the same direction as your toes.
When you feel a deep stretch in your inner thigh, push yourself back up to standing by squeezing your glutes and quads, returning to the starting position
Alternate sides and repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Side Plank - CM
desc: The Side Plank is a great isometric core exercise that mostly works on your obliques and shoulder stability while also activating the outside of your glutes
cues: Maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout the exercise.
Engage your core muscles and avoid allowing your hips to sag or rotate.
steps: Lie on your side with your legs extended and one forearm supporting your upper body. Your elbow should be directly under your shoulder.

Stack your feet on top of each other and lift your hips off the ground, forming a straight line from your head to your heels. (option to stagger your feet if you need a little more help with your stability)
Engage your core and hold the position for the desired duration.
Repeat the exercise on the other side.

name: Sidelying Clock
desc: Side-Lying Arm Circles are a dynamic stretching exercise that targets your shoulders and upper body. It's like you're drawing circles in the air while lying on your side, improving shoulder mobility and flexibility.
steps: Begin by lying on your side with your legs at 90 degrees
Reach as far forward as you can with your top arm, and trace the largest circle you can through your fingertips
Don't allow your knees to come off the ground, it's okay if you can't make contact with your fingers for the entire rotation
Follow your rotating hand with your eyes for the entire movement

name: Single Arm Preacher Curl
desc: The Single Arm Preacher Curl is an excellent exercise for isolating each bicep individually, promoting focused muscle engagement and symmetry.
cues: Curl the weight smoothly, concentrating on the bicep contraction.
Control the descent, fully extending your arm without locking the elbow.
steps: Sit at the preacher bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing up.
Starting with your weaker arm, place your upper arm against the pad and extend your arm without locking out your elbow
Curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder, squeezing the bicep at the top.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Complete all reps on one arm before switching to the other.

name: Single Arm Reverse Pec Deck
desc: The Single Arm Rear Delt Fly is an isolation exercise that targets the posterior shoulder while allowing you to really dial in mind-muscle connection and address left-to-right imbalances. Great for shoulder health, posture, and upper-back aesthetics.
cues: Think “reach long, then sweep wide”
Keep your shoulder down and away from your ear
Slight bend in the elbow the entire time
Move slow and controlled – no momentum
steps: Set up machine seat so the handle is in line with your shoulder position when sitting.
Sit sideways on the seat, so you need to reach across your body to grab the handle. You should start with your weaker arm first.
Grab the handle keeping your chest squared forward. Brace your core and maintain a neutral spine.
Initiate the movement by pulling your arm out and back, keeping the shoulder packed down.
Pause briefly and feel the rear delt contract.
Slowly return to the start position under control, maintaining tension.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
muscles: Posterior Deltoids Upper back (rhomboids, mid traps) Rotator cuff (stabilization)

name: Single Leg Bridge - CM
desc: The Single Leg Bridge is one of my favourite zero-equipment exercises for the glutes.
cues: Drive your heel through the floor.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Lift one leg off the ground, keeping it extended straight in front of you.
Push through your heel on the ground to lift your hips toward the ceiling, focusing on squeezing your glute.
Lower your hips back down to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Avoid hyperextending your lower back; instead, focus on engaging your glutes.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.

name: Single Leg Extension
desc: Leg Extensions are a quad BURNER. Try to focus on getting a good squeeze through your quads rather than trying to move heavy weight
cues: Squeeze your quads at the top of the movement.
Think about pulling your butt into the seat while pointing your toes up towards your face.
steps: Sit on the leg extension machine with your back flat against the seat and your legs positioned under the pads. The pad should be just above your ankles.
Extend your weaker leg upward, focusing on squeezing your quadricep at the peak of the movement.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position. Avoid letting the weight all the way down to maintain tension in your quads.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions on your first leg before starting on your second.

name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
desc: The Single-Leg Glute Bridge is an advanced variation of the traditional glute bridge, designed to intensify glute and hamstring engagement by isolating one leg at a time. This exercise enhances unilateral strength, improves pelvic stability, and challenges your core, making it excellent for correcting muscle imbalances and boosting overall lower body strength.
cues: Drive through your heel of the "grounded" foot to maximize glute activation.
Keep your hips level to prevent rotation and engage your core.
Squeeze your glutes at the top as if holding a coin between them.
Maintain a straight line from your shoulders to your knee at the top of the movement.
Avoid pushing through your toes
steps: Starting Position: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Prepare for Lift: Extend one leg straight out, keeping both thighs aligned.
Engage Core and Glutes: Press the heel of your planted foot into the ground.
Lift Hips: Raise your hips toward the ceiling by squeezing your glutes, ensuring your extended leg stays in line with your torso.
Achieve Alignment: Lift until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to the knee of your supporting leg.
Hold Momentarily: Pause at the top for a brief moment, focusing on keeping your hips level.
Lower with Control: Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position without letting them touch the ground completely.
Repeat Repetitions: Complete the desired number of reps on one side before switching to the other leg.
subs: Glute Bridge: For a less intense variation that works both legs simultaneously.
Single-Leg Hip Thrust: Similar movement pattern but performed with your upper back elevated on a bench.
Bulgarian Split Squat: To target the glutes and legs in an upright position.

name: Single Leg Hamstring Curl
desc: The Single Leg Hamstring Curl is great for isolating out each of your hamstrings to promote balanced muscle growth
cues: Squeeze your hamstrings at the top of the movement.
Drive up through your heel.
Keep your core braced to avoid moving your lower back.
steps: Position yourself on the single leg hamstring curl following the positioning instructions on the machine.
Curl your leg upward, focusing on squeezing your hamstrings at the peak of the movement.
Avoid arching your back and maintain control throughout the exercise.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position, feeling the stretch in your hamstrings.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.

name: Single Leg RDL Load Into Rotation
desc: Use a kickstand

name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift
desc: The Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift is a challenging strength and balance exercise that targets the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back.
cues: Reach up and back with your hips
Pretend that you're dragging the weight down your shins
Reach for the wall behind you with your hips
steps: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart and your knees slightly bent, holding either dumbbells or a barbell
Shift your weight to your left leg while extending your right leg straight behind you.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the movement.
Maintain a slight bend in your left knee as you hinge further into the movement
Your back and extended leg should remain in a straight line.
Reverse the motion by squeezing your glutes and hamstrings to return to the starting position.

name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift (Warmup)
desc: The Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift is a challenging strength and balance exercise that targets the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back.
steps: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Shift your weight to your left leg while extending your right leg straight behind you.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the movement.
Maintain a slight bend in your left knee as you hinge further into the movement
Your back and extended leg should remain in a straight line.
Reverse the motion by squeezing your glutes and hamstrings to return to the starting position.

name: Single-Leg Leg Press
desc: The Single-Leg Leg Press is a variation of the traditional leg press exercise, performed with one leg at a time. This exercise targets the lower body muscles, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes, with an emphasis on unilateral (one-sided) strength and muscular balance.
cues: “Press through the platform” (pushing eventos throughout your full foot)
Lower the platform in a controlled manner, keeping your knee in line with your foot.
steps: Sit on the leg press machine and place your non dominant (or less strong) foot near the center of the footplate. (Different foot positions can have different effects but the standard is great!)
Adjust the seat or platform so that your knee is bent at a 90-degree angle at the start.
Press the platform away by extending your knee and hip, but avoid locking your knee at full extension.
Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the weight as you lower it.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.

name: Sissy Squats
desc: Sissy Squats are a bodyweight quad isolation, one of my favourites over quarantine!
cues: Keep your glutes and abs squeezed the entire time, keeping your core RIGID
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and come up to balance on your toes. You can hold onto something with a hand for balance.
With your glutes and abs squeezed to keep a neutral spine, drop your knees forward toward the ground.
Push through your toes to come back to standing
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Sit-Ups
desc: The Sit-Up is a classic abdominal exercise that targets your abs.
cues: Squeeze your abs, thinking about bringing your rib cage closer to your pelvis as you sit-up
Control the descent and avoid using momentum to lift your torso.
steps: Begin by lying on your back with your knees bent and your feet wedged under heavy dumbbells or a couch.
Place your hands behind your ears or across your chest.
Engage your core to lift your upper body off the ground, bringing your torso toward your knees.
Slowly lower your torso back down to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the descent.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on controlled breathing and proper form.

name: SkiErg - CM
desc: The SkiErg is a full-body conditioning exercise that emphasizes powerful pulling through the upper body while demanding strong core engagement and efficient hip drive. It’s excellent for building engine capacity, grip strength, and total-body coordination.
cues: Drive down with your lats, not just your arms
Hinge at the hips – don’t squat
Keep your ribs down and core braced
Finish tall before the next pull
Smooth and rhythmic, not frantic
steps: Set the damper to a moderate setting and grab the handles with a neutral grip.
Stand tall with a slight bend in the knees and arms extended overhead.
Initiate the pull by engaging your lats and hinging at the hips.
Drive the handles down toward your thighs as your hips snap forward.
Keep your arms long until the final portion of the pull, then finish with the triceps.
Return the handles overhead under control while standing tall and relaxed.
Reset your posture and repeat in a smooth, continuous rhythm.

name: Skull Crushers - CM
desc: Skull Crushers, also known as Lying Tricep Extensions, are a strength exercise that targets the triceps muscles at the back of the upper arm. They are typically performed with a barbell, EZ curl bar, or dumbbells while lying on a bench.
cues: Keep your elbows stationary and pointing straight up throughout the exercise.
Lower the weight towards your forehead or just above it in a controlled manner.
Extend your arms fully at the top, focusing on squeezing your triceps.
Avoid flaring your elbows out to the sides to maintain focus on the triceps.
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your feet planted on the floor.
Grip the weight (barbell, EZ curl bar, or dumbbells) with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms above your chest, keeping your wrists straight.
Keeping your elbows fixed in place, bend your elbows to lower the weight towards your forehead or just behind your head.
Stop just before the weight reaches your head.
Extend your arms back to the starting position, contracting your triceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
desc: The Smith Machine Bench Press is an effective exercise for targeting your chest, emphasizing overall chest strength and muscle development.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Think about trying to snap the bar like a piece of spaghetti
steps: Set the bench  under the Smith Machine with the bar directly over where your lower chest will be.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip just outside shoulder width. Think about trying to snap the bar in half
Lift and release the bar, and slowly lower the bar to touch your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Smith Machine Incline Bench Press
desc: The Smith Machine Incline Press is an effective exercise for targeting the upper chest, emphasizing overall chest strength and muscle development.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Think about trying to snap the bar like a piece of spaghetti
steps: Set the bench to a 30-45 degree incline under the Smith Machine with the bar directly over where your upper chest will be.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip just outside shoulder width. Think about trying to snap the bar in half
Lift and release the bar, and slowly lower the bar to touch your upper chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift
desc: The Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift is a controlled variation of the classic Romanian Deadlift. The fixed bar path helps guide your movement, making it easier to maintain proper form and isolate the hamstrings and glutes. This variation is particularly useful for beginners learning hip hinging mechanics, or for more advanced lifters who want to safely overload the posterior chain.
cues: Keep your chest tall and shoulder blades pulled back as you hinge. Push your hips back like you’re closing a car door behind you. Maintain a slight bend in the knees—don’t let them lock out. Keep the bar close to your legs throughout the movement. Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes at the top.
steps: Adjust the Smith Machine bar to about mid-thigh height and load with desired weight. Stand with your feet hip-width apart, bar resting against your thighs, and grip it with both hands overhand. Unlock the bar and take a small step back so you’re balanced under the bar path. Begin the movement by hinging at the hips—push them backward while keeping your spine neutral and bar close to your legs. Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings (usually just below the knees). Reverse the movement by driving your hips forward, standing tall, and squeezing your glutes at the top. Repeat for the desired number of reps, then carefully re-rack the bar.
subs: Barbell Romanian Deadlift Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift Hip Thrust

name: Smith Machine Row (Pronated)
desc: The Smith Machine Row is an effective exercise for targeting the back muscles, particularly the lats and rhomboids. This exercise helps build upper body strength and muscle mass, enhancing overall back development.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Drive through your elbows, thinking of your hands as hooks
Think about breaking the bar like a piece of spaghetti
steps: Stand facing the Smith Machine, feet shoulder-width apart, and grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees and a straight back throughout the movement.
Pull the bar towards your upper abdomen, leading with your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Keep your chest up and your core engaged for stability.
Control the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
desc: The Smith Machine Shoulder Press is an effective exercise for targeting your shoulders with minimal injury risk.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Think about trying to snap the bar like a piece of spaghetti
steps: Set the bench slightly less than a 90-degree angle, positioned so there will only be a couple inches between your chest and the bar.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip just outside shoulder width. Think about trying to snap the bar in half
Lift and release the bar, and press the bar up until your elbows are nearly locked out.
Slowly lower the bar to the starting position, keeping tension in your shoulders.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before reracking

name: Smith Machine Squats
desc: The Smith Machine Squat is a controlled, machine-based squat variation that targets the lower body, particularly the quads, glutes, and hamstrings. By using the guided track of the Smith Machine, this exercise provides added stability, making it ideal for those looking to isolate leg muscles without worrying about balance.
cues: Keep an even center of pressure throughout your full foot. Not too much through the toes, not too much through the heels!
Keep a tight brace the entire time to support your lower back.
Control the descent and avoid bouncing at the bottom.
Keep your knees tracking directly in line with your toes. They shouldn't be caving in or going too wide out.
steps: Position yourself under the bar of the Smith Machine, setting it at shoulder height.
Stand with your feet slightly in front of you, about shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core
Unrack the bar by twisting it off the safety hooks and lower yourself into a squat, keeping your knees aligned with your toes.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, ensuring control throughout the movement.
Drive through your full foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
subs: Barbell Back Squat – for more core activation and free-weight control.
Leg Press – for a similar lower-body stimulus with back support.
Goblet Squat – for a more functional squat pattern with a free weight

name: Spider Curls
desc: Spider Curls are an isolation exercise performed on an incline bench, targeting the biceps. They challenge your biceps most in a fully contracted position.
cues: Let your arms fully extend at the bottom of the curl.
Curl the weight up with control, focusing on the bicep contraction.
steps: Lie prone (face-down) on an incline bench, with your torso against the bench and feet on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, letting your arms hang straight down.
Curl the weights towards your shoulders, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.

name: Stairmaster
desc: The Stairmaster is a cardio and endurance exercise machine that simulates the action of climbing stairs. It's a popular choice in gyms for cardiovascular workouts and lower body strengthening.
cues: Maintain good posture; keep your back straight and shoulders back.
Use your legs to power your movement, rather than leaning heavily on the handrails.
Engage your core for balance and stability.
Step fully onto each step to engage your glute and thigh muscles more effectively.
steps: Start with a moderate pace and gradually increase as your fitness improves. Mix intervals of higher and lower intensities for a varied workout. Pay attention to your form to avoid strain or injury. Use the handrails for balance but not for support; relying on them too much can reduce the effectiveness of the workout.

name: Stationary Lunge - CM
desc: Stationary Lunges are a great lower body warmup that help build stability in your hips and develop your legs.
cues: Keep an even center of pressure in your front foot. Think of the “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Keep your front knee tracking in line with your middle toe. Your knee cap should point in the same direction as your toes.
Screw your front foot into the floor. Your left foot should screw in counterclockwise when it's in front and right foot screwing in clockwise when it's in front.
steps: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart.
Take a step forward with your weaker foot.
Lower your body by bending both knees, making sure your front knee stays over your ankle, and doesn't cave in.
Continue descending until your back knee hovers just above the ground or lightly touches it. Both of your knees should be at a 90 degree angle
Push through your front foot to return to the starting position.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement, keeping your chest open and your core engaged.
Perform the desired number of repetitions on one leg, then switch to the other.
subs: Heel Taps (for Hip and Ankle Stability)

name: Stationary Lunges (Warmup)
desc: Stationary Lunges are a great lower body warmup that helps stabilize the hips and build some heat in the body. Use a hand support for balance if needed
cues: Keep an even center of pressure in your front foot. Think of the “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Keep your front knee tracking in line with your middle toe. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
Screw your front foot into the floor. Your left foot should screw in counterclockwise when it's in front and right foot screwing in clockwise when it's in front.
steps: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart.
Take a step forward with your weaker foot.
Lower your body by bending both knees, making sure your front knee stays over your ankle, and doesn't cave in.
Continue descending until your back knee hovers just above the ground or lightly touches it. Both of your knees should be at a 90 degree angle
Push through your front foot to return to the starting position.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement, keeping your chest open and your core engaged.
Perform the desired number of repetitions on one leg, then switch to the other.
subs: Heel Taps (for Hip and Ankle Stability)

name: Suitcase Carry - CM
desc: Estimate the distance. The Suitcase Carry is a core and stability exercise that's great for bullet proofing your back!
cues: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning to one side.
Think about walking like a robot out of terminator
Maintain a neutral spine and avoid excessive twisting.
steps: Stand upright with a dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand, arm fully extended by your side.
Engage your core and keep your shoulders level.
Walk forward for the desired distance or time, keeping your torso straight.
Once you get half way, switch the weight to the other hand and walk back to the starting position with good posture.

name: Suitcase Lunges
desc: Suitcase Lunges are a dynamic lower body exercise that targets the hamstrings, glutes, and quads and work on your core stability.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
PULL yourself forward using your front leg to emphasize your hamstring and glute
Keep your front knee over your ankle.
steps: Start by standing with your feet hip-width apart, a single dumbbell or kettlebell in either hand.
Take a step forward with your strongest leg, lowering your body by bending your both knees until your back knee hovering just above the ground. This should ideally be one smooth motion
Ensure your front knee stays over your ankle, and is at a 90-degree angle. Your back knee should also end up at a 90-degree angle.
Pull through your front heel using your hamstring and glute to return to the starting position.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement, with your chest open and core engaged.
Alternate legs each repetition.
Hold the weight in your opposite hand on the next set.

name: Sumo Deadlift
desc: The Sumo Deadlift works virtually every muscle in your body, but focuses mostly on your gluteus medius (outer glutes) and quads. Sumo deadlifts put less pressure on your lower back than conventional deadlifts.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Keep an even center of pressure across the “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Push your knees out to keep your kneecaps pointing in the direction of your middle toes. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line.
Screw your feet into the floor, left foot screwing in counterclockwise and right foot screwing in clockwise
“Spread the floor” (you can imagine standing on wet newspaper that you’re trying to split down the middle)
Squeeze your glutes like you're trying to crush a walnut
Make your armpits disappear by squeezing your triceps into your lats
steps: Set your feet in a wide stance (wider than shoulder width) with your toes pointed out at 45-degrees. Your shins should be 1 inch away from the bar.
Push your knees out, keeping your hips close to the bar, and chest proud. Lower yourself down until you can reach the bar.
Grab the bar at shoulder width, and try to snap it in half.
Take a breath in like you're going to dive underwater and brace your core

"Pull the slack" out of the bar before bringing your hips forward between your knees and shoulders, maintaining your brace and neutral spine (think of it as a horizontal movement, not a vertical movement)
Pause briefly at the top before pushing your knees out, while maintaining a proud chest until you lower the bar back to the starting position
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Sumo Squats
desc: The Sumo Squats a version of squats that targets more of the inner thigh and the outside of your glutes
cues: Push your knees out and squeeze your glutes on the way up
Maintain a proud chest while leaning forward
Brace your core like someone is going to poke you in the stomach
steps: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and toes pointed outward at a 45-degree angle.
Hold a weight in front of you in between your legs
Push your knees out as you squat down, keeping your weight evenly distributed through your feet and maintaining a neutral spine.
Push through your feet to return to the starting position, focusing on keeping your knees wide.
Avoid rounding your back and maintain control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Sun Salutations
desc: Sun Salutations, also known as "Surya Namaskar" in yoga, are a series of flowing movements that create a dynamic sequence to awaken and energize the body. They combine various poses and stretches to promote flexibility, strength, and mindfulness.
steps: Begin in Mountain Pose (Tadasana) with your feet together, palms pressed together in front of your chest.
Inhale and raise your arms overhead, arching slightly backward (Mountain to Upward Salute).
Exhale and bend forward, bringing your hands to the floor (Forward Fold).
Inhale, lift your chest, and extend your spine forward (Halfway Lift).
Exhale and step or jump back into Plank Pose.
Lower yourself down into Chaturanga Dandasana (Low Plank) with your elbows bent.
Inhale as you transition into Upward-Facing Dog (Upward Dog) with your chest up and thighs off the ground.
Exhale, lift your hips, and press back into Downward-Facing Dog (Downward Dog).
Inhale and step or jump your feet forward, returning to Forward Fold.
Exhale as you fold deeper.
Inhale, raise your arms, and come back to Upward Salute.
Exhale, bringing your hands to your heart in Mountain Pose.
muscles: Full Body - Comprehensive workout involving multiple muscle groups.
Focus on Core, Shoulders, Hips, and Legs.
subs: Core 4 on the Floor + Handcuff with Rotation

name: Supermans - CM
desc: Supermans are a bodyweight exercise that targets the lower back, glutes, and upper back muscles. This exercise is great for improving the strength and stability of your spine.
cues: Imagine you're flying through the air like superman!!!!
Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
steps: Lie face down on a mat or the floor with your arms extended straight out in front of you.
Keep your legs extended and together.
Lift your chest, arms, and legs off the ground as high as comfortably possible while squeezing your glutes and lower back.
Hold the top position for a moment, feeling the contraction in your lower back and glutes.
Lower your chest, arms, and legs back down to the ground with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Supinated Lat Pulldown
desc: The supinated lat pulldown is a variation of the classic lat pulldown exercise. It emphasizes your biceps and middle of your back. You can think of the "supinated" wrist postition like holding a bowl of "soup"
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Drive through your elbows, thinking of your hands as hooks
steps: Grab the bar at shoulder width
Keep your shoulder blades down and back (in your back pockets) for the entire exercise
Drive down through your elbows, trying to SQUEEZE your lats
Raise the bar back up with control, still keeping your shoulders down and back

name: Supported Stationary Lunge
desc: Stationary Lunges are a great lower body warmup that help build stability in your hips and develop your legs.
cues: Keep an even center of pressure in your front foot. Think of the “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Keep your front knee tracking in line with your middle toe. Your knee cap should point in the same direction as your toes.
Screw your front foot into the floor. Your left foot should screw in counterclockwise when it's in front and right foot screwing in clockwise when it's in front.
steps: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart, holding a support with either hand.
Take a step forward with your weaker foot.
Lower your body by bending both knees, making sure your front knee stays over your ankle, and doesn't cave in.
Continue descending until your back knee hovers just above the ground or lightly touches it. Both of your knees should be at a 90 degree angle
Push through your front foot to return to the starting position.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement, keeping your chest open and your core engaged.
Perform the desired number of repetitions on one leg, then switch to the other.
subs: Heel Taps (for Hip and Ankle Stability)

name: Supported Step Back Lunges
desc: Alternating Step-Back Lunges are a dynamic lower body exercise that can help improve leg strength, balance, and coordination
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
PULL yourself forward using your front leg to emphasize your hamstring and glute
Keep your front knee over your ankle.
steps: Start by standing with your feet hip-width apart, holding a support with one or both of your hands.
Take a step back with your strongest leg, lowering your body by bending your front knee until your back knee hovering just above the ground. This should ideally be one smooth motion
Ensure your front knee stays over your ankle, and is at a 90-degree angle. Your back knee should also end up at a 90-degree angle.
Pull through your front heel using your hamstring and glute to return to the starting position.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement, with your chest open and core engaged.
Alternate legs each repetition.
subs: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift With Kickstand

name: Suspension Trainer High Row
desc: The TRX High Row targets your upper back and biceps while engaging your core and shoulder stability. This exercise variation emphasizes flaring your elbows outwards during the movement.
cues: Maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Keep your core engaged throughout the movement.
Initiate the row by pulling your elbows back and flaring them outward.
steps: Adjust the suspension trainer straps to chest height.
Stand facing the anchor point, holding one handle in each hand, walk backwards until you're standing upright with the suspension trainer taut when held up to your chest
Walk your feet forward, with your arms fully extended.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core.
Pull your elbows back, flaring them out so they are in line with your ears
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Pause briefly, feeling the contraction in your back muscles.
Slowly extend your arms, returning to the starting position with control.

name: Suspension Trainer High Row (Elbows Flared)
desc: The TRX High Row with Elbows Flared targets your upper back and biceps while engaging your core and shoulder stability. This exercise variation emphasizes flaring your elbows outwards during the rowing motion.
cues: Maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Keep your core engaged throughout the movement.
Initiate the row by pulling your elbows back and flaring them outward.
steps: Adjust the suspension trainer straps to chest height.
Stand facing the anchor point, holding one handle in each hand, walk backwards until you're standing upright with the suspension trainer taut when held up to your chest
Walk your feet forward, with your arms fully extended.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core.
Pull your elbows up and back, so your elbows are at the same height as your ears.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Pause briefly, feeling the contraction in your back muscles.
Slowly extend your arms, returning to the starting position with control.

name: Suspension Trainer ITY
desc: The Suspension Trainer ITY is a dynamic exercise that targets your upper back, and rear shoulders. This movement combines three distinct positions to engage multiple muscle groups.
cues: Maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core throughout the exercise.
Move smoothly between the ITY positions.
Keep your shoulder blades down and back.
Control the straps with your hands.
steps: Adjust the suspension trainer to chest height.
Stand facing the anchor point, holding one handle in each hand.
Begin in the "I" position, arms extended overhead.
Transition to the "T" position, arms out to the sides.
Move to the "Y" position, arms forming a Y shape in front of you.
Return to the "I" position and repeat the sequence.
Maintain tension on the straps throughout the exercise.
Perform the desired number of repetitions.

name: Suspension Trainer Inverted row (legs elevated)
desc: Inverted Row (Legs Elevated) The Legs Elevated Inverted Row is the next step up from the legs extended version. Putting your heels up on a bench instead of the floor makes your body more horizontal, which means you're lifting more of your own bodyweight on every rep. Only your heels stay on the bench.
cues: Pull your elbows into your back pockets, not out to the sides.
Imagine you're trying to snap the handles apart as you pull. You won't, but your upper back will fire a lot harder.
Squeeze your glutes like you're holding a full glass of water on your hips that you can't spill.
The more horizontal your body is, the harder it gets. To make it easier, go back to the legs extended version with your heels on the floor.
steps: Set the straps so the handles hang around waist height and grip one in each hand, palms facing each other.
Place a bench in front of you, sit down under the handles and put your heels up on the bench, then lean back until your arms are straight and there is tension in the straps.
Extend your legs straight out with only your heels on the bench, then drive your hips up so your body forms a straight line from your heels to your shoulders.
Pull yourself up by driving your elbows back until the handles reach your ribs.
Pause for a second at the top and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself back down slowly, letting your shoulder blades spread apart at the bottom for a full stretch.
Keep your hips up the entire set. The moment they sag, you're done.
muscles: Glutes and Core (holding your hips up)

name: Suspension Trainer Inverted row (legs extended)
desc: Inverted Row (Legs Extended) The Legs Extended Inverted Row is the next step up from the bent-knee version. Straightening your legs puts your feet out in front of you instead of underneath you, which means you're lifting more of your own bodyweight on every rep. Only your heels stay on the floor.
cues: Pull your elbows into your back pockets, not out to the sides.
Imagine you're trying to snap the handles apart as you pull. You won't, but your upper back will fire a lot harder.
Squeeze your glutes like you're holding a full glass of water on your hips that you can't spill.
The more horizontal your body is, the harder it gets. Stand more upright to make it easier, or go back to the bent-knee version.
steps: Set the straps so the handles hang around waist height and grip one in each hand, palms facing each other.
Walk your feet forward and sit back until your arms are straight and you're leaning back with tension in the straps.
Extend your legs straight out in front of you with only your heels on the floor, then drive your hips up so your body forms a straight line from your heels to your shoulders.
Pull yourself up by driving your elbows back until the handles reach your ribs.
Pause for a second at the top and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself back down slowly, letting your shoulder blades spread apart at the bottom for a full stretch.
Keep your hips up the entire set. The moment they sag, you're done.
muscles: Glutes and Core (holding your hips up)

name: Suspension Trainer Low Row
desc: The Suspension Trainer Low Row is an excellent exercise for targeting your back and biceps while also engaging your core for stability. This exercise uses suspension straps, making it a versatile addition to your workout routine. Weight=Number of steps you take forward from the starting position
cues: Maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Think about driving your elbows backwards, your hands are hooks!
steps: Adjust the suspension trainer straps to chest height.
Stand facing the anchor point, holding one handle in each hand, walk backwards until you're standing upright with the suspension trainer taut when held up to your chest
Walk your feet forward, with yourarms fully extended.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core.
Pull your elbows back, bringing your hands toward your ribcage.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Pause briefly, feeling the contraction in your back muscles.
Slowly extend your arms, returning to the starting position with control.

name: Suspension Trainer Pistol Squat
desc: The Suspension Pistol Squat is a challenging lower-body exercise that's great for building stability and progressing to unassisted pistol squats.
cues: Find something that's still and stare at it.
Keep a braced core the entire movement.
Use your legs as much as possible, with your hands as an as-needed assist
steps: Stand facing the anchor point, holding the handles in front of you with tension throughout the suspension trainer.
Lift one foot off the ground, extending it straight out in front of you.
Slowly bend your standing leg and lower your body down into a squat, aiming to get your thigh parallel to the ground.
Use the TRX straps for balance and support as you lower and raise your body.
Push evenly through your full foot on your standing leg returning to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.
muscles: Ankles and Calves (for balance and stability)

name: Suspension Trainer Pushups
desc: Suspension Trainer Pushups are a challenging variation of pushups that involve using suspension straps or a TRX system to increase instability and engage your core muscles.
cues: Tuck your shoulder blades into your back pockets (shoulder blades down and back)
SQUEEZE your hands and core for extra stability
steps: Adjust the suspension straps to an appropriate height and hold one handle in each hand.
Face away from the anchor point with the handles tucked in near your armpits and walk your feet forward until the trainer is fully tensed.
Walk backwards, counting the number of steps you take. The more steps you take back, the more challenging it will be.
Maintain a straight line from your head to your heels, engaging your core.
Lower your chest toward the handles while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Keep your shoulder blades back and down throughout the exercise.

name: T-Pushups
desc: T-Pushups are a challenging variation of traditional pushups that engage the chest, shoulders, and core while also promoting rotational strength and stability.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back through the pushup portion
Imagine that your planted hand is literally rooted into the ground
Keep your plant hand shoulder "packed down" (shoulder blade down and back)
steps: Begin in a standard pushup position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body to the ground, maintaining a straight line from head to heels.
Push up to the starting position.
Rotate your torso and lift your right arm off the ground, opening your chest to the side.
Hold the "T" position for a moment.
Return your right hand to the ground.
Repeat on the other side, rotating and lifting your left arm.
Maintain a controlled pace throughout.

name: Techno Gym Low Pull
desc: The Techno Gym Low Pull is a versatile machine exercise that targets your back muscles, particularly the lats, while also engaging the biceps and rear shoulders.
steps: Begin by sitting at the machine with your chest against the pad and gripping the handles.
Keep your back straight and shoulders down as you pull the handles towards your lower chest. Focus on squeezing your back muscles at the peak of the movement.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position, controlling the descent.

name: TechnoGym Bicep Curl
desc: The Technogym Bicep Curl similar to other machine bicep curls is a great way to isolate and target the biceps.
cues: Keep the back of your arm flat against the supporting pad
SQUEEZE your biceps, at the top, and slowly lower the weight back down
steps: Adjust the seat and arm pad to a comfortable position, ensuring your elbows align with the machine's axis.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, keeping your palms facing upward.
Curl the handles toward your shoulders, focusing on squeezing your biceps.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly extend your arms back to the starting position.
Control the movement throughout, avoiding any jerking motions.
Repeat the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Technogym Artis Squat
desc: The Technogym Artis Squat is a specific type of squat exercise performed using the Technogym Artis line of strength equipment. This machine is designed to simulate the natural movement of a squat while providing additional safety and stability. The Technogym Artis Squat machine typically features ergonomic designs and advanced biomechanics to enhance the squatting experience.
cues: Keep your back straight and chest up throughout the exercise.
Push through your full foot, thinking about pushing your feet "through the platform".
Ensure your knees are aligned with your feet and do not buckle inward.
steps: Position yourself on the Technogym Artis Squat machine, adjusting the equipment according to your height and comfort.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart or slightly wider, toes slightly pointed out.
Pull the lever and squat down to adjust the bottom position of the machine. You want the largest range of motion you are comfortable controlling.
Push through your full foot to come to the top, avoiding locking your knees out completely.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Pull the lever to release the weight and return to the starting position.

name: Technogym Core
desc: The Technogym Abdominal Machine is tailored to strengthen and build the abdominal muscles through a controlled range of motion, ensuring effective targeting of the core area.
cues: Engage your core before starting each rep like you're going to be punched in the gut.
Exhale as you perform the crunch or contraction phase, enhancing core engagement.
Maintain a slow and controlled movement to increase the effectiveness of the exercise.
Avoid pulling with your neck or shoulders; the movement should originate from your abdominals.
steps: Adjust the machine to fit your body size, ensuring that when seated, the pads or levers are positioned correctly according to the machine design.
Sit or lie down on the machine, positioning your feet under support pads or on footrests.
Grip the handles or position your arms according to the machine’s design, typically either behind your head or across your chest.
Perform the abdominal contraction by curling your upper body towards your knees, maintaining a focus on engaging the abs throughout the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining tension in your abdominal muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions and sets.

name: Technogym Shoulder Press (Neutral Grip)
desc: The Technogym Shoulder Press with a neutral wrist position is a machine-based exercise targeting the shoulder muscles, specifically designed to optimize shoulder muscle engagement while minimizing undue stress on the wrist joints. The neutral grip typically means your palms are facing each other during the press, a position that can be more comfortable for the wrists and shoulders.
cues: Keep your back flat against the seat throughout the exercise.
Press the weight up smoothly, focusing on using your shoulder muscles.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement.
Control the weight on the way down, not letting the stack touch down between reps.
steps: Adjust the seat of the Technogym Shoulder Press machine so that the handles are at or just below shoulder level.
Sit back with your back flat against the pad, grasping the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Brace your core and press the handles upwards until your arms are almost fully extended.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
muscles: Upper Pectorals (Upper Chest, to a lesser extent)

name: Testing
desc: Push your knees out Alternative exercise: conventional deadlifts

name: Thread The Needle
desc: Thread the Needle is a yoga-inspired stretch that targets the shoulders and upper back. It helps improve mobility in the shoulder joint and releases tension in the upper body.
steps: Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position.
Inhale and reach your right arm up toward the ceiling, opening your chest.
Exhale and thread your right arm under your left arm, reaching it across the floor.
Lower your right shoulder and cheek to the ground, feeling the stretch in your right shoulder and upper back.
Return to the tabletop position and repeat on the other side, lifting your left arm and threading it under your right arm.

name: Tibialis Raise
desc: The Tibialis Raise is an exercise that targets the tibialis anterior muscle, which is located on the front of your lower leg. Strengthening this muscle can help improve ankle stability and prevent shin splints.
steps: Lean your butt against a wall with your heels two foot lengths away from the wall
Raise your toes as high as you can off the wall, hold for a couple seconds and slowly lower them back down
Repeat

name: Trap and Rhomboid Trigger Point
desc: The Trap and Rhomboid Trigger Point helps to alleviate tension and discomfort in your upper back while increasing range of motion.
steps: Begin by pinning a lacross ball against a wall where your trap meets your rhomboids (see video)
Begin rolling back and forth in the area looking for tender spots
Once you find a tender spot, try to add pressure to the area using the lacross ball while leaving your muscle relaxed
Spend 5-10 seconds relaxing into the position, then make very small movements over the tender spot for 5-10 seconds
To intensify the trigger point, your can lift your arm directly overhead and then across your body to your hip to lift your shoulder blade off your back, continuing to look for tender spots
Find another tender spot, and repeat

name: Trapbar Deadlift
desc: The Trapbar Deadlift works virtually every muscle in your body, but focuses mostly on your hamstrings, glutes, and lower back.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Keep an even center of pressure across the “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Keep your kneecaps pointing in the direction of your middle toes. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
Screw your feet into the floor, left foot screwing in counterclockwise and right foot screwing in clockwise
“Spread the floor” (you can imagine standing on wet newspaper that you’re trying to split down the middle)
Squeeze your glutes like you're trying to crush a walnut
steps: Stand inside the trapbar with your shoelaces in line with the sleeve of the bar (directly in the middle of the bar)
With vertical shins, and a neutral spine, reach back with your butt until your hands can reach the bar
Grab the bar in the middle of the handle
Take a breath in like you're going to dive underwater and brace your core

"Pull the slack" out of the bar before bringing your hips forward between your knees and shoulders, maintaining your brace and neutral spine (think of it as a horizontal movement, not a vertical movement)
Pause briefly at the top before reaching your butt back into a hinge pattern, returning the bar to the ground with vertical shins and a neutral spine
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Tricep Kickback
desc: Tricep Kickbacks are one of the most humbling tricep exercises. They are great for isolating your triceps, but be ready to grab some small dumbbells!
cues: Keep your elbow as high in the sky as you can
Squeeze and hold at the top
steps: Start the exercise holding the dumbbell in your non-dominant hand
Place your non-dominant hand and knee on a bench to support yourself.
Raise your dominant elbow as high as you can while maintaining good upper body posture.
Extend your arm back, fully straightening your elbow.
Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.

name: Tricep Stretch
desc: Tricep Stretch is a static stretching exercise that targets the triceps, helping to improve flexibility and alleviate tightness in the back of the upper arms.
steps: Stand next to a wall or vertical surface, with your feet about hip-width apart.
Raise one arm straight up and bend it at the elbow, reaching your hand down your back.
Reach up the wall with your elbow, while trying to bring your armpit closer to the wall

name: Unilateral Stepups
desc: Unilateral Stepups are an effective lower body exercise that targets the quads, hamstrings, and glutes, while working a ton on your lower body stability.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
Keep an even center of pressure across your plant foot “foot tripod” (your heel, big toe, and little toe)
Keep your kneecaps pointing in the direction of your middle toes. Your knee shouldn’t be shifting towards your mid line or too far out.
Try to be as quite as possible when touching your back foot down.
steps: Stand facing an elevated platform or bench.
Step onto the platform with one foot, ensuring your whole foot is firmly planted.
Push through your full foot to lift your other leg to the point it's hovering over the platform.
Step back down with control and return to the starting position. Your foot should touch down very softly.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions on your first leg before switching to your next.

name: Upper Trap Trigger Point
desc: The Upper Trap Trigger Point helps to alleviate tension and discomfort in your upper traps while increasing range of motion.
steps: Begin by sitting with a tall posture, with your shoulders down
Try to find a point in your upper traps that is tender, and slowly apply pressure by pinching the area
Spend 5-10 seconds relaxing into the position, then make very small movements over the tender spot for 5-10 seconds
To intensify the trigger point, tilt your head away from the trigger point, and rotate your head
Find another tender spot, and repeat

name: V-Bar Lat Pulldown
desc: The V-Bar Lat Pulldown is a variation of the classic lat pulldown exercise that emphasizes a little more of the middle of your back and forearms.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Drive through your elbows, thinking of your hands as hooks
steps: Using a V-bar attachment, sit on the Lat Pulldown machine with your knees secured under the pads.
Maintain a slight arch in your lower back and keep your chest up throughout the movement.
Pull the v-bar down towards your collarbone, focusing on engaging your back muscles.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom of the movement.
Control the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Walking Cooldown
desc: Great workout today!!! We're going to just cool down the body and add a bit of routine to the end of your workout. Take a moment to soak in that you just did something phenomenal for your body!!! Input the speed you walk as the "other number"

name: Walking Lunges
desc: Walking Lunges are a dynamic lower body exercise that targets the hamstrings, glutes, and quads. This exercise enhances leg strength, balance, and coordination.
cues: Keep your core squeezed like you're going to be poked hard in the stomach
PULL yourself forward using your front leg to emphasize your hamstring and glute
Keep your front knee over your ankle.
steps: Start by standing with your feet hip-width apart, holding weights down by your sides if appropriate.
Take a step forward with your strongest leg, lowering your body by bending your both knees until your back knee hovering just above the ground. This should ideally be one smooth motion
Ensure your front knee stays over your ankle, and is at a 90-degree angle. Your back knee should also end up at a 90-degree angle.
Pull through your front heel using your hamstring and glute to return to the starting position.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement, with your chest open and core engaged.
Alternate legs each repetition.

name: Walking Warmup
desc: A brisk walk is a great way to build some heat in the body before you workout. Physically warming up your body literally decreases your injury risk! Input the speed you walk as the "other number"

name: Wall Balls - CM
desc: Wall Balls are a full-body conditioning movement that combines a squat with an explosive overhead throw. They build leg strength, power, coordination, and cardiovascular capacity while rewarding good rhythm and efficiency.
cues: Let your legs do the work – arms guide the ball
Stay tall through your chest at the bottom of the squat
Use one smooth motion from squat to throw
Breathe out as you throw
Catch soft and immediately descend into the next rep
steps: Stand facing the wall holding the medicine ball at chest height, feet about shoulder-width apart.
Squat down, keeping your heels on the floor and chest upright.
Drive through your legs to stand up explosively.
As you rise, use your momentum to throw the ball upward toward the target on the wall.
Fully extend your hips, knees, and ankles at the top of the movement.
Catch the ball softly as it comes down, absorbing it into your next squat.
Descend immediately into the next rep to maintain rhythm.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Wall Circles
desc: Wall Circles are one of my personal favourite upper body warmups, since it will help to improve your shoulder mobility AND stability.
steps: Stand with your side facing a wall, about a foot away.
Place the back of your nearest hand against the wall at shoulder height, with your fingers splayed.
PUSH into the wall for a couple seconds, and then move your hand up the wall, pausing to PUSH again
When your hand is pointing straight up, flip your hand over so the palm of your hand is flat against the wall, still spreading your fingers
Work your way down the wall, pausing to PUSH into your hand
Once your hand is lower than shoulder height, flip back around to the back of your hand and start again
Try to maintain a proud chest, and tall posture throughout

name: Wall Posture Sequence
desc: Wall Posture Sequence is a series of posture movements that will help you stand taller with your shoulders back :)
steps: Stand with your back against a wall, arms pointed down at 45 degrees
Raise your arms to point UP at 45 degrees. Repeat 10 times.
Return to the starting position with your arms pointed down at 45 degrees
Bring your hands in to give yourself "earmuffs", then return to the "45 degree" position. Repeat 10 times.
Hold your hands down by your sides.
Alternate raising each arm up as high as you can, like you're trying to climb a ladder. Repeat 10 times on each side.

name: Weighted Chin-Ups
desc: Weighted Chin-Ups are an advanced variation of chin-ups that involve adding extra weight to the exercise, increasing the resistance and intensity.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
steps: Secure the desired amount of weight around your waist using a weight belt OR hold a dumbbell between your legs
Grasp the bar with your palms facing you, your hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar, focusing on engaging your back muscles.
Lower yourself down with control until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Weighted Dips
desc: Dips are a great way to target your chest, triceps, and shoulders while building upper body strength.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
To target more chest, think about leaning forward, to target more triceps, think about keeping your feet forward
steps: Using a weight belt or holding a dumbbell in between your legs, position yourself on parallel bars with your arms fully extended.
Lean slightly forward and lower your body by bending your elbows until you feel a deep stretch in your shoulders and chest.
Push yourself back up to the starting position, keeping your chest engaged.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Weighted Pull-Ups
desc: Weighted Pull-Ups are an advanced variation of pull-ups that involve adding extra weight to the exercise, increasing the resistance and intensity.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
steps: Secure the desired amount of weight around your waist using a weight belt OR hold a dumbbell between your legs
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, your hands just wider than shoulder-width apart.
Pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar, focusing on engaging your back muscles.
Lower yourself down with control until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Weighted Unilateral Hip Opener
desc: The Weighted Unilateral Hip Opener is a great way to improve your squat depth, and is used by a ton of high level athletes
steps: While holding a light weight, begin by kneeling on one knee with your opposite foot positioned the same as you would for a squat.
Keeping your outside foot flat on the ground, chest up and your back straight, push your outside knee out over your toes, allowing the weight to pull you deeper into the stretch
Come back to the starting position, and repeat, trying to get a deeper stretch in your ankles, hips, and groin with each cycle

name: Weighted Windmill
desc: Windmills are a dynamic exercise that focuses on rotation of the spine and stability of the shoulder
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart
Hold a weight straight overhead, like you're trying to touch the ceiling
Start by hinging your hips backwards, and reach down to the floor with your free hand (holding your weighted arm straight up)
Try to keep your legs relatively straight to stretch your back and hamstrings
Reverse the motion by engaging your core and lifting your torso back up to the starting position, still keeping your raised hand high!
subs: Lizard with Rotation + Shoulder Taps (warmup substitution)

name: Wide Grip Cable Row
desc: The Wide Grip Cable Row is an effective exercise for targeting the back muscles, particularly the lats and rhomboids, with an emphasis on the upper back. This exercise helps build strength and muscle mass in the back, contributing to overall upper body development.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Drive through your elbows, thinking of your hands as hooks
steps: Sit on the cable row machine and grasp the wide grip handle, sitting up tall with your knees slightly bent.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the movement.
Pull the handle towards your upper abdomen, leading with your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Maintain a stable posture without leaning back excessively.
Control the handle back to the starting position, extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
subs: Dumbbell Bent Over Row with Wide Elbows

name: Wide Grip Neutral Lat Pulldowns
desc: The Wide Grip Neutral Lat Pulldown is a variation of the classic lat pulldown exercise that emphasizes a little more of the outer muscle fibers of your back and forearms.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Drive through your elbows, thinking of your hands as hooks
steps: Using a wide neutral grip attachment, sit on the lat pulldown machine with your knees secured under the pads.
Maintain a slight arch in your lower back and keep your chest up throughout the movement.
Pull the bar down towards your collarbone, focusing on engaging your back muscles.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom of the movement.
Control the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Wide Grip Pushup
desc: Wide-Grip Pushups are a variation of traditional pushups that emphasize the chest muscles.
cues: Keep your shoulders down and back, like you're trying to pinch a pencil between your shoulder blades
Think about keeping your shoulder blades in your back pockets (down and back)
Maintain a proud chest
Think about screwing your hands into the floor, left hand screwing in counterclockwise and right hand screwing in clockwise
steps: Begin by placing your hands slightly wider apart than a traditional pushup, only wider by about a hand's width.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them at a slightly wider angle than regular pushups
Go as low as your flexibility allows while maintaining your shoulders down and back.
Push up through your palms to return to the starting position.

name: Windmills
desc: Windmills are a dynamic stretching exercise that focuses on rotation of the spine and stability of the shoulder
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart
Hold your right hand straight overhead, like you're trying to touch the ceiling
Start by hinging your hips backwards, and reach down to the floor with your left hand (keeping your right hand straight overhead)
Try to keep your legs relatively straight to stretch your back and hamstrings
Reverse the motion by engaging your core and lifting your torso back up to the starting position, still keeping your raised hand high!

name: Windshield Wipers
desc: The Windshield Wiper Stretch is a dynamic stretch that helps improve mobility and flexibility in your hips and lower back. It's a great way to release tension and increase range of motion.
steps: Begin sitting on the ground, with your feet shoulder width, knees at 90 degrees, and your hands behind you to support your position
Leaving your feet and butt on the ground, lower your knees to the left until you feel a good stretch, and then reverse,  and go in the opposite direction!

name: Wrist Stretch Sequence
desc: This sequence is perfect for stretching your wrists and forearms. It’s especially helpful if you’re experiencing stiffness in your forearms or elbow discomfort, which can often be linked to tightness in the wrists and forearms. For best results, try these stretches on a turf or yoga mat.

name: Zottman Curls
desc: Zottman Curls are a unique variation of the traditional bicep curl, combining a regular curl with a reverse curl. This exercise targets both the biceps and the forearms.
cues: Keep your elbows pinned at your sides throughout the movement.
Rotate your wrists smoothly as you transition between the curl and the reverse curl.
Control the descent, especially during the reverse curl portion, to maximize forearm engagement.
Maintain a steady, controlled pace without using momentum.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length.
While rotating your palms up, perform a regular bicep curl.
At the top of the curl, rotate your wrists so your palms face down.
Lower the dumbbells in this reverse curl position.
At the bottom, rotate your wrists back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
subs: Dumbbell Bicep Curls + Reverse Wrist Curls
